古乐是个谦谦君子，擅抚琴却不擅言语，仇越海知道，也总喜欢逗他。\n我与你烈言兄弟:
Gu Le was the kind of refined soul whose emotions flowed effortlessly through his guqin, yet whose tongue seemed to stumble over every word. Qiu Yuehai knew this well and loved teasing him.
"If your brother Lie Yan and I both fell into the river, who would you save?"
Pluck! The absurd question made Gu Le miss a note.
"Both! I'd save both!"
"Impossible. With your frame, saving one would be a miracle enough."
"Then... ah..." Flustered, Gu Le could only sigh.
"Must you two drown yourselves at all?"

When they first met, Gu Le saw a fisherman-looking youth lounging on a rooftop, golden wheat stalk between his teeth. Bright sunlight that day. The stalk inside his mouth gleamed like gold. Newly recruited by Lie Yan to resist the Khitans, Gu Le squinted upward:
"Excuse me... is Brother Lie Yan here?"
"Brother Lie Yan? You two sound close? Are you his real brother?"
The youth's teasing eyes sparkled with mischief.
"No... we're not related, it's just..."
"Stepbrothers then?"
"No... No relation at all! I was playing guqin when Lie Yan..." Red-faced, Gu Le gave up explaining and let his head drop.
"Anyway, he asked me to come."
The youth laughed, jumping down.
"I know, I know. Another recruit against the Khitan! I am here for that too. I'm Qiu Yuehai. Call me brother if you like."
Qiu Yuehai patted his shoulder, perhaps an apology.
"Sorry, but whenever I meet earnest young gentlemen like you, I can't help wanting to tease you."

Later, when they became famed as two of the "Eight Talents of Hedong," their bond deepened. The refined aristocrat and the rough fisherman were modern Zhong Ziqi and Bo Ya. Their dynamic became legendary:
Gu Le struggles to explain, always starting with "Anyway..."
Qiu Yuehai instantly understood: "What he means is..."
Others called them the "Anyway" and "What he means" brothers. Such was their harmony. Their youthful camaraderie burned bright. What came after belongs to another story.
古乐没想到自己会和仇越海到这一步。\n就像没想到当初会和他成为知音好友。\n这段:
Gu Le never imagined things would end this way with Qiu Yuehai.
Just as he never imagined they'd become bosom friends in the first place.
Their friendship had begun in an unexpected way and now ended in one too—such is the capriciousness of fate, beyond human reckoning.

It all started with the girl's request before she left: Don't tell Qiu Yuehai.
It wasn't that they had a quarrel. She just didn't want to drag him into danger."If Big Brother Yuehai knew, he'd charge headlong after me," she'd said with a laugh.
"But you—you've always been restrained."
Yes. Restrained. And so, restrained as ever, Gu Le kept her secret. Watched her leave. Then lost her trail entirely.
The girl's whereabouts became a mystery—one he couldn't bring himself to share with Qiu Yuehai.
Why? First, he'd promised. Second, the guilt was too heavy.

He'd intended to reveal the truth once he found answers himself. So when Qiu Yuehai turned away, Gu Le stayed silent and vanished into the jianghu alone.
Years later, after untold hardship, he finally uncovered the answer.
But when he gathered the girl's bones gently into his arms, he realized the truth was even harder to confess than the mystery itself.
Some lies become lifelong burdens.
All he could do was watch Qiu Yuehai leave in anger, heave a long sigh, and bury the story's bitterness in his own heart.

叶万山铁心将军的名号，最初是那些敬仰他的百姓给他的。\n铁心二字，是军心如铁、刚:
Ye Wanshan, the man known as General Ironheart, earns his title from the people who admire his unyielding spirit.
"Ironheart" encapsulates his firm resolve and unshakable will that refuses to bend. Even when his beloved wife and daughter are captured by the Khitan and used as leverage against him, he does not waver. His family is torn apart, yet he never once thinks of surrendering.
Their sacrifice was justified if it meant ensuring the peace of his city and safeguarding its people.
But even with that conviction, the city still fell.
The Khitan's forces were too strong, their numbers too overwhelming. Despite his relentless efforts, the Ding nation was lost.

On the day Ye Wanshan ordered his troops to retreat, the truth settled heavily upon him: one man alone could not defend a nation or reclaim what had been lost. He could only wait for the reinforcements of the imperial army to march north alongside him.
And so, he waited for thirteen long years. Thirteen years of suffering, of torment that never ceased, only to be broken by the rhythm of his sword swings. With each strike, his resolve grew harder.
At long last, the opportunity he had been waiting for arrived: Emperor Shizong's northern expedition.

Donning his well-maintained armor once again, he rallied his Tigers in Chains and stood at the city walls, awaiting the main forces.
But to his shock, the northern expedition was called off midway.

How could this happen? 
How could they just abandon the campaign?
His wife, daughter, and son were gone, and the people of the border city had suffered for far too long, yet the expedition was halted. How could they stop?
It was unacceptable. If the cowards hiding in the rear wouldn't march north, Ye Wanshan would lead them himself.

He turned his horse, his blade now aimed not at the enemy but at the very citizens of the city. A thick black cloud blotted out the sun, and in that heavy, oppressive silence, his face remained unreadable. 
He had made up his mind: If sacrificing the lives of a city's people could restore peace, then so be it.
That night, no enemies came to the gates. Yet, someone saw the Khitan entering the city, and the cries of agony echoed through the city where Ye Wanshan had lived for thirteen years.
His iron resolve, once full of care, now turned cold and callous.

Later, retreating to the Qinghe Buddhist Temple in search of some semblance of peace, Ye Wanshan encountered a monk who spoke of crossing the Bodhi Sea of suffering to reach the blissful shore.
But he knows the truth: This sea of suffering is too vast, too deep, and he can never cross it.

同光三年，八月二十五日\n自六月积雨，七十五日方停，门中心忧黄河，命我出山一探。:
August 25, Year 3 of Tongguang
The torrential rains that began in the sixth month have finally stopped after seventy-five days. Worried about the Yellow River, Mohist Hill ordered me out to investigate. The Elder gave me a thousand taels of silver for disaster relief. Why a thousand? Ten would be enough. Beyond the mountain, there are always people eager to "deliver money" to my door.

August 26, Year 3 of Tongguang
Encountered refugees. Gave them ten flatbreads; spent one tael.

August 27, Year 3 of Tongguang
Encountered refugees. Gave out twenty-five flatbreads; spent two taels and five qian.

August 28, Year 3 of Tongguang
Encountered refugees. Gave out thirty flatbreads; spent four taels. Blast it, grain prices are soaring. Where are the bandits, and where is my coin purse?

August 29, Year 3 of Tongguang
Encountered refugees. Gave out eighteen flatbreads. My own money is exhausted, and I haven't seen a single bandit.

August 30, Year 3 of Tongguang
The world is vast, and my stomach is empty. Not a bandit in sight. I miss Mohist Hill, I miss the Elder, and I miss those nine hundred and ninety-nine taels of silver.

August 31, Year 3 of Tongguang
Still no bandits. I pawned my outer coat a while ago. It matters not; the fire of hunger burns so fiercely I don't feel the cold.

September 1, Year 3 of Tongguang
Hungry. Heard there was a bandit camp in the mountains. I rushed there in ecstasy, only to find the ground littered with the starved dead. After running around for half a day, all I got was a cracked bowl. I, too, have become a refugee.

September 2, Year 3 of Tongguang
Hungry. Met a young man by the Yellow River named Feng Nengqi. His swimming skills are phenomenal. He can navigate the currents with ease while carrying sandbags and catch fish barehanded. I am so envious.

September 3, Year 3 of Tongguang
Famished. Feng Nengqi actually recognized my Mohist mechanisms and wants to learn our mechanical arts. How can the secrets of Mohist Hill be taught so casually? What an insolent and insincere fellow.

September 4, Year 3 of Tongguang
Ate three fish. Feng Nengqi said he wants to learn mechanisms to repair the river dikes. Though his character is commendable, Mohist arts must never be shared with outsiders...

September 5, Year 3 of Tongguang
Ate five fish. This man is a piece of uncarved jade; it would be a true pity not to sculpt him. I permitted him to travel with me. I often toy with my gadgets and let him figure them out on his own. The quiet joy in this is something I cannot explain to others.

君不见是个小偷，但是有文化的小偷。\n出生时，君不见的父母因常听一些喝醉的书生吟:
Jun Bujian was a thief, but a cultured thief. 
When he was born, his parents often overheard drunken scholars reciting lines like "Have you not seen the Yellow River's waters descending from the heavens?" Thinking it sounded refined, they named him Jun Bujian ("Have You Not Seen"). Later, he looked up the poem himself and fell in love with one particular phrase: "Heaven bequeaths me talents." If wealth is heaven-sent, he reasoned, then taking a little isn't really stealing, is it? 
Now, in Weiyang City, Jun Bujian has his eyes on a young nobleman: Wen Wuhen. The kind who seems shrewd but is actually the easiest to rob, and whose coin, in terms of steamed buns, could feed hundreds. 
When they meet again seven days later, Wen Wuhen is half-dead from hunger. Jun Bujian can't fathom why the boy refuses to return home, even when starving. Pity that the money he'd lifted from him is long gone, spent on others. All he has left is a single moldy bun. 
Eventually, he learns the truth: Wen Wuhen hates his family. The "Wen" ("Warm") Manor is anything but. So Jun Bujian makes a promise: "Next birthday, I'll treat you to fresh white-flour buns." It's the first warmth Wen Wuhen has ever known. 
Today is Wen Wuhen's birthday, and Jun Bujian leaves early. Meanwhile, Wen Wuhen, knowing his friend loves magic tricks, steals a manual on Five Ghosts Command from his family vault, planning to surprise him. But in Jun Bujian's dingy hideout, he finds something else: his own stolen identity plaque. 
So he was the culprit all along, Jun Bujian! Betrayed, Wen Wuhen vows to kill him. Because he'd trusted him. Yet Jun Bujian never returns. 
Wen Wuhen went back to the Wen family. After four of its six heirs perished under mysterious circumstances, he became its head. Meanwhile, Jianghu buzzed about a new Master Thief who calls himself "Heaven's Bequeathed Talent." Every year, on Wen Wuhen's birthday, the thief appears, steals his favorite gift in plain sight, and then gives it back.

听闻今日开封府尹留在宫中吃饭，尚食局的吴御厨总算放下心来。要她说，官家的城府也太:
Word had it that the Kaifeng Prefect would be staying in the palace for a meal today, and at last Chef Wu of the Culinary Office could breathe a little easier. If you asked her, His Majesty was far too hard to read.

Her family had served in the palace since Tang times. Their specialties ranged from Divine Roast, made from just four liang taken from a whole sheep and said to ward off summer heat, to Brahman Cloud Buns, Checkerboard Pastries, and Twenty-Four Solar-Term Wontons. It did not matter who sat on the throne. As long as someone had to eat, they would need her family's craft. Only by pleasing the Son of Heaven's palate could they keep a dependable roof over their heads through decades of upheaval.

Who could have guessed that the present emperor's tastes would be harder to read than a needle at the bottom of the sea? Whether she sent up Scarlet Honeyed Delights, the satisfyingly chewy Little Heavenly Crisps, or the silky White Dragon Stew, His Majesty never seemed to remember any one dish for long. Anything carried to his table came back to her with plates and cups scraped clean. Even the more than seventy lifelike steamed flour figures she had made purely for display, not a single one was left.

She asked the steward about it and got only one answer: "He ate them."

He ate them? Steamed flour figures were made to look pretty. Who would eat those? She could never get a proper sense of this ruler's tastes, and it left her with no end of needless worry.

Still, once the Kaifeng Prefect began staying in the palace for meals more often, she finally got some response. The Prefect was a man of taste. If she prepared dishes suited to the season and added a little ingenuity, she could usually win his praise. Whenever that happened, His Majesty would chime in with a few words like "Not bad, not bad," as a token compliment to the chef.

Perhaps her efforts to vary the menu had become too obvious, for the Prefect eventually asked about it. She did not dare hide anything and explained the whole matter from beginning to end. The man at the table looked as though he wanted to smile but was holding it back. After a moment's thought, he called her over and quietly gave her a few instructions. Chef Wu's expression turned strange as well, and she withdrew, hesitant.

That day, the Kaifeng Prefect again remained with His Majesty discussing affairs until noon, and the meal was served as usual. This time, two large bowls of coarse white porcelain were brought in, both steaming hot.

One bowl held three liang of hui mian. The noodles were pulled thin. When lifted with chopsticks, they stretched long with a lively spring, while the milky mutton broth ran down the strands, gleaming in the sunlight like a pale ribbon of jade. A few slices of plain boiled mutton, cut to just the right thickness, lay spread across the top like a cover waiting to be lifted. Beside them floated a small mound of bright green scallions, drifting restlessly about. The moment the mutton was moved aside, the fresh scent of broth and scallion rose with the steam and went straight to the nose, making one's eyes drift back to the bowl again and again. For people of the Central Plains, one of the gravest sins is to let a good bowl of thin, clear, piping-hot noodles sit until it turns soft and soggy.

The other bowl held a full four liang. These noodles were pulled thick, the solid sheets of dough almost as thick as the bowls that held them. Bite into them, and there was the deep satisfaction of feeling your front teeth and canines work through them inch by inch. This bowl held double the mutton, not sliced, but chopped. Fresh-cut pieces sat in the broth, cooked until they curled up tight. The first bowl had a clear broth. This one was glossy with red chili oil. Fat might normally feel greasy on the tongue, but boiled through in scalding-hot mutton broth, it turned into a steaming, glistening pool of temptation. Even simple greens, once they fell into that broth, came up coated in a sheen of oil that would not come off. In an imperial chef's eyes, the cooking fat common in farm kitchens was hardly elegant. But some things taste all the better for not trying to be refined.

His Majesty reached out, took one bowl, and at once bent over it, slurping away. The palace attendant behind him, holding a jade tray, jumped. The Prefect waved a hand, and the attendant hurriedly brought the garlic on the tray over to the Prefect instead. The Prefect split the bulb and set the cloves on the table. His Majesty picked one up, bit into it skin and all, hissed, spat out the skin, and kept eating without even looking up.

The younger brother shot his elder brother a look, then dutifully began peeling the garlic. His elder brother might not care about such things when eating, but he still intended to.

Still, good as mutton-broth noodles were, the meal would have been even better with a few cold dishes to cut the richness. So at last, one final attendant brought up a plate of dressed green leaves: jingjie, grown near Kaifeng, a fragrant herb just right for the season. By rights it should have been to the Prefect's taste, yet at the sight of it he frowned slightly and, without seeming to, nudged the plate toward His Majesty instead.

Hearing the movement, His Majesty looked up and grinned.

"Why, it's jingjie. And such a huge plate of it."
"Mhm."
"Go on, have some. Don't be picky."
"Quit nagging me. I'm not eating it."
"You're a grown man already..."
"If you like it so much, eat it yourself."
"Just one bite. One bite, and the two of us can say we've had a big plate of jingjie."

The Prefect had been guarding his bowl, but at that line he could not help laughing.

"You've eaten so many imperial dishes, and you did not even spare the flour figures. How does that not count as having seen the world? Barely anyone gets to taste that much."
"How was I supposed to know they weren't meant to be eaten? Besides, they were made with good flour. Wouldn't it have been a waste to let them go bad?"
"You ate dozens of them, and you still weren't full?"
"Not all at once. I wasn't full. I just got badly choked up by the end. Drank a lot of water."
"Next time, give them to other people."
"Yeah... I still can't get used to it. I always feel like leftovers are mine."
"Not the worst habit."
"How so?"

The younger brother thought of it and nearly lost his composure, quickly lowering his head to his noodles to hide his smile.

"Tell us," a young palace maid in the Culinary Office could not help asking the same question His Majesty had. "Chef, what did the Prefect say to you? Does His Majesty like noodles?"

"He said..." Chef Wu's expression turned strange again, her nose wrinkling. "His Majesty is... easy to feed."
"Easy to feed?"

The maid and the chef looked at each other. They had seen Sons of Heaven who demanded rare delicacies, phoenix marrow and dragon liver. But a Son of Heaven who was easy to feed?

Thunderclap Society is the palace's cricket-fighting club. We have put our notes and hard-won tricks into this booklet for fellow enthusiasts. This month's issue is penned by the Verdant Strider of the Rear Garden. Comments are welcome.

In cricket-fighting, "catch, raise, fight" are the three essentials. But how do you pick the right champion for your jar? We are curious too. We want to know.

Part I: Judging a Cricket

We invited Lord Fan of the Ministry of War to share his tips on sizing up a fighter.

"To judge a cricket is to judge a general. If your eye is bad, you lose before the match even starts.

"I have been in office for over a decade, served through two reigns, and still managed to keep my footing. That is all from knowing how to read people. Crickets work the same way.

"Start with head color, then wing color. Check the neck, and use the body tone as a final clue. Some are called 'one-glance overlords': rugged heads, bulging brow marks, a hard temper that will not bend. Fighters like that often have sharp, hooked jaws, made to pierce an opponent's head casing. They win more often than not.

"Others look steady and plain, the rust-grey type that never shows off. Small, maybe, but their staying power is rare. Charging first and breaking through is courage. Taking a hit to lure the enemy in is brains. People come in all kinds, and so do crickets."

Editor's Note:
There is no end to learning. If I can learn Lord Fan's way of reading both people and crickets, then I can stay at the bottom of the cricket world without getting knocked out.

Part II: Feeding and Rearing

This section is sponsored by Little Zhangzi's AAA Palace-Supply Cricket Feed.

"Raising a cricket is like being on duty. Your methods have to be right, and the little fellow has to be tough. Some amateurs, hungry for a win, feed their crickets chili. Do not do that.

"If you want your fighter to flip the other one in the ring, remember two words: fresh and slow.

"Fresh means changing the feed every day.
"Slow means building it up bit by bit. No rushing.

"And since we are here, I recommend my own Carrying-Pole Cricket Feed. Honest nourishment, solid stuff. Limited stock, get it while you can."

Editor's Note:
Sponsorships are still welcome for this section.

Part III: Master Q&A

Interviewee: "Cloud Gazer"
Editor: Master Zhan, as the top cricket fighter in the inner palace, what do you make of all these schools mixing it up?

Cloud Gazer: "Different schools, different moves. Bite. Throw. Lift. Pinch. Hook. Drag. Roll. Press. Those are all tactics a cricket can use.

"It is the same as two masters trading blows. You win when strength, brains, and technique come together.

"A cricket's world is one little jar. Do not make your own world even smaller than that.

"If you cannot even tell what kind of fighter your cricket is, let it go now. Do not send it into the ring just to die for you.

"Winning and losing are small things. The point is to let the kings meet, trade moves, and learn some sportsmanship. Alright. I have carpentry to get back to."

Squeak... Creak...
Amidst the roar of boiling water and the marketplace din, Little Letian could always pick out that one sound: the groan of the wooden He'le press clamping down.
Squeak... Creak...
Another bowl of noodles slid free. His mother swept her left hand beneath the press, steady and practiced, while her right tipped a ladle of sauce over the noodles. A fresh bowl was ready.
Little Letian was convinced that everyone pressed he'le noodles differently.
His father's pressing had sounded light and lively, like wood breathing.
Once, his father took him into the mountains. A breeze passed through the pine forest, and his father told him to press his ear against the trunk. The sound he heard was exactly the same as when father made noodles, soft, hollow, alive.
After his father passed away, Little Letian never once saw his mother cry.
He watched his mother, who used to be very quiet, learn to call out to customers, raising her voice to praise how fresh her sauce was, and how springy the noodles were.
Then she would reach for a bowl, swift and sure, and slide it beneath the press.
Squeak... Creak...
Little Letian knew that sound now. It wasn't wood breathing anymore, but wood crying.

For most of my life, I have dwelt within Hidden Mountain. Over time, the voices of woods and ravines, of all things sounding together, have slowly become familiar to my heart.
I still remember my first entry through the mountain gate. Standing at the #YMountain Verge#E, I heard the sound of grasses and trees putting forth new shoots, so faint and delicate that it seemed like music from Heaven itself. To this day it still lingers in my heart. That first stirring in the heart was what later led me to found the Harmony Troupe.
Though I later served at #YDeepwave Works#E, the pure notes of those companions who once sought harmony with me, and the ringing force of the debates at #YConfluence Gazebo#E, have never for a single day fallen silent in memory.
Yet as the years passed and all things changed, each went his own way, and meetings and partings alike became hard to foretell.
Still, as the seasons turn and sound and scene follow one another, a thought has taken root. Why not fashion a device that preserves sound?
If wisdom shares one law with wood and stone, then man and mechanism may dwell in accord as well.
The Mohists do not prize music, yet neither do we reject the five tones. We take the people's livelihood as our root, and the arts as secondary.
Now I wish to set the thought of the Mohist Dao to the rhythms of the natural world, and by means of this sound-preserving device, record once more the everyday soundscape of Mohist Hill.
Perhaps it may preserve the beauty of the present hour, and also leave to those who come after an unanswered question that has long remained in my heart.

That question is this: what sound does the Mohist Dao make?

If I may hear it but once in this lifetime, that will be enough.
And yet the Mohist Voice is abundant as rivers and seas, while my own life is faint and slight as the trace of grass.
In but a moment, my hair has turned white. One by one, all sounds grow still. Only the little cat in my #Ystudy#E gives the occasional soft cry, keeping me company in these fading years.
Among those who study after me, many now dispute the roads of opening the mountain and sealing the mountain. I fear the harmony of many voices once heard upon #YSeven-Hued Plain#E may never again be found.
If someone should come after me, willing to take up this casket and continue the search for the Mohist Voice, then my heart... would be greatly comforted.

周威烈王二十三年，夏雨如倾，黄河溢，洛水崩。\n三月间，二十七处堤坝告急，三千墨:
In 403 BC, the summer rains came down in torrents. The Yellow River overflowed, and the Luo burst its banks.
In the third month, twenty-seven dikes stood on the verge of collapse. Three thousand Mohists were sent out to the breach sites, bearing earth and stone on their backs to fill the gaps, laboring through the night without rest. Yet for all the strength the Mohists spent, it was still no more than a cup of water thrown on a blazing cartload of firewood.
At that time, the king was enfeoffing Han, Zhao, and Wei. Lords and nobles gathered in glittering array, the rites resplendent, pipes and drums shaking the heavens. When Mozi heard of it, he put on his coarse robe, stepped out into the frost, and hurried to the Zhou capital, hoping to admonish the rulers and save the world. But those exalted lords saw only the fat of sacrificial beasts within their cauldrons, never the floating corpses beyond the hall. Instead they spoke of the waxing and waning of Heaven's Dao, of what no human power could resist, and drove him out for disturbing the sacred order. Mozi cried out in grief: was human life truly worth less than Heaven's decree?
Yet Mozi would not let the matter rest. He went among the villages, teaching the common people how to dredge channels and guide the waters. But those willing to learn were pitifully few. The people did not think to save themselves. Instead, they bound young boys and girls and cast them into the river, praying to Heaven for mercy. Everywhere he went, it was the same.
That night, the flood ran wild, drowning the lands of the Nine Provinces. Millions perished. Mozi wept amid the ruined walls, and at last understood this: if Heaven's decree was the flood, then the hearts of men were the dam. This was not the fault of the feudal lords alone, nor of the common people alone. It was the fault of Heaven. To clear a blocked river is easy. To clear a blocked heart is hard. A river is dredged by opening its course. A heart is dredged by breaking through its ignorance. And so he set his will upon Beholding Heaven and Denying Fate.
Gongmeng Zigao urged him, saying, "If Heaven's decree is a lock, it has stood fast for a thousand years. The rise and fall of Xia, Shang, and Zhou were all explained in its name. If you would break through that barrier, I fear it cannot be done within a single age."
Mozi was unmoved. He said, "A lock of a thousand years must be opened with a key of a thousand years. If ten years fail, if a hundred years bear no fruit, then what is there to fear in a thousand?"
Gongmeng Zigao urged him again. "It is not that there are none beneath Heaven who reject fate, but how few dare say so aloud. Why is that? Have you not heard? The feudal lords use Heaven to rule the people. The hundred schools use Heaven to uphold their teachings. The common people take Heaven as their faith. Would you make yourself the enemy of all under Heaven?"
Mozi said, "The feudal lords fear Heaven because they fear losing their mandate to rule. The learned fear Heaven because they fear losing their principles. The common people fear Heaven because they fear losing their lives. But when men's hearts are blocked and their lives are bound to Heaven, how can one retreat merely because of fear? In ages past, Yu the Great cut through Longmen and opened the Nine Marshes, not for his own sake. Now, since no one else will stand forth to deny Heaven, then the Mohists must go first. If it is for the benefit of the world, what is one life to a Mohist?"
Gongmeng Zigao bowed and asked, "What then will you do?"
Mozi said, "From this day onward, the Mohists shall strip the heavens of their mystique and lay the sky plain before all eyes. Though it take a thousand years, ten thousand years, we shall teach the world to know that thunder is not Heaven's wrath, rain is not Heaven's lament, and Heaven's decree is nothing to fear."

呵，可惜啊，假得连三岁小孩都糊弄不了！: Too bad. A toddler could see through this fake.

呵，把他们抓起来保护？: Oh, you "captured" them for their own protection?

呵，是嫌我死得太慢了么？: Am I not dying fast enough for you?

呵，曲子词有什么难，走着瞧！: Heh, what's so hard about lyrics? Just wait!
呵，有本事我们换围棋！: Heh, if you dare, let's play Go!

呵，死相……手、手——: Heh, you bad boy... hey, my hand—

呵，没想到，这开封府内，还有人藏在暗处。: Hmph, I didn't expect hidden players in Kaifeng's courts.
呵，游侠撞人的本事倒不小。: Quite the talent for bumping into people.

When it played in the snow with a human, the person kept muttering about “boundaries."

Boundaries? What are those? Liangzhou is nothing but snow. Since when did snow have edges?

The Snow Lion didn't understand.

The one who used to have the most fun with it had slipped away lately. And now there was another Snow Lion at its side, cold as ice and no fun at all.

Being able to warm up to people was rare enough. Who knew you could love too much and make them worry?

Just to dodge the Snow Lion's hugs, humans would wrap themselves in snow, shiver through the cold, and pretend to be one of its kind.

Snow Lions good. Humans bad. Fine, fine.

At least in the end, the human could stand shoulder to shoulder with the Snow Lion and quietly watch the snow fall.

哼，那不然你来问问？: Hmph, why don't you give it a try then?
哼，那个小丫头就罢了。: Oh, just forget about that little girl.

哼，那偷走毒方的叛徒，其实你也了然于心了吧！: Hmph. You knew who stole the poison formula all along, didn't you?

哼，那就撕了这美人图！: Then tear up the portrait of the beauty!
哼，那就让我们三个出手，给你编一个最长的长命缕！: Hmph, then we'll make you the longest one ever!
哼，那就让我考考你这后学。: Let's see what you've learned, youngster.
哼，那我毕胜也是个鼎鼎有名的江湖大侠，便上前同它往来了两句，寻思将来罩着它，收个: Naturally I, Bi Sheng, a name known across the jianghu, offered to take it under my protection.

哼，都是群不要命的莽撞货！: Hmph. A bunch of fools throwing their lives away!

哼，除了你还能有谁？: Who else could it be but you?

唉......以前，咱们的刀是用来护佑百姓的。现在刀上沾的，都是百姓的血。: Sigh... Our blades used to shield the innocent. Now they're slick with their blood.
唉~反正有大把时光~: We have all the time in the world!
唉~古来征战几人回！！！: How many warriors ever make it home?
唉~这等小事，少侠何不自己来呢？成了风媒，全天下的消息都尽在你的掌握之中~线人耳: Why not just join us? You'd have informants everywhere, news from all corners of the land... Finding someone would be a breeze!
唉——天子疑心，有些真相，我们明白却说不得。: Sigh... the emperor is a suspicious man. Some truths... we know, but we're not allowed to speak.
唉……上半场就完了？那我？: It's over already? What about me?
唉……不是舞的事儿。: Alas, it's not a matter of dancing.

唉……他到底是什么意思嘛……: Ugh... What is he really trying to say?
唉……休沐之日，我本不愿破戒。: Sigh... On an official rest day, I'd rather not break the rules.

唉……刚刚……好像有鱼……: Hah... just now... felt like a bite.

唉……对不住，对不住，我也是一时气恼。: Sorry about that. I got a little carried away.
唉……小叶子这丫头，我是管不住了。: Sigh... Little Leaf just doesn't listen anymore.

唉……我到底那一日才能回城啊！: **Sighs**... When will I finally get back to the city?
唉……我当二十不得意，一心愁谢如枯兰。: Sigh... At twenty I'd found no place in the world, and my heart withered like a dead orchid.
唉……我昨夜点灯时，照见将军鬓间的白发，竟那般扎眼了……原来将军也真的会变老啊。: Sigh. Last night when I lit the candle, I noticed the General's sideburns had gone completely white… Even the General grows old in the end.
唉……我都开始好奇了，他们两个到底谁更厉害一点呢？: Well... Now I'm actually curious. Who's really better at it?
唉……时运不济，带了一车货途径此地，没曾想被绿林打劫了去: *sigh* Luck's not on my side. I brought a carriage full of goods through here, and it was robbed by bandits.
唉……是我多言了，游侠保重。: Ah... I'm going on too much. Take care, wanderer.

唉……梨花还会再开吗……: **Sighs**... Will the pear blossoms bloom again?
唉……此人就在里面，你若不信，就自己见识见识吧。: *sighs*... That person is inside. Better if you just go see for yourself.

唉……真放心不下我的研究啊……啁啾啊，一定砸中啊……: Can't stop worrying about my research... please hit the target...
唉……神仙渡……唉……离人泪……唉……: Alas... Heaven's Pier... alas... Parting Tears...
唉……等要走时，给这儿留几柱香火吧。: Ah… when we leave, let's light some incense here.
唉……算了算了，反正匕见将军吃了也不会怎样……: Alas... oh well, Dagger General won't do any harm anyway...
唉……经阁已被贼人所破，那口佛钟早已跌入玉池，无所寻觅了。: Alas... the scripture pavilion has been ransacked by thieves, and the Buddhist bell has long since fallen into the jade pool, nowhere to be found.
唉……能活着有口吃的，够不错了。: *sigh* Being alive and having food is enough.
唉……若有一丝马虎，折的可不是咱的颜面，是朝廷的体统啊……: One slip and it won't just be our heads on the line, it'll be the court's reputation.
唉……若能再快点就好了……: Sigh... If only we could finish even sooner...
唉……虽早已猜到故人长绝，但终究令人伤怀……游侠，你且看看这封信。: I always knew, deep down. But it still hurts to hear it. Here, read this.

唉……这一天天的，煮了一锅又一锅，连个回头客都没有。: Day after day, pot after pot, and not a single customer comes back for seconds.
唉……这怎能细看……尽是赔本。: ...Better not look too closely at the books. They're all in the red.
唉……造什么凌云轨，费木头费时间的。: The Skytouch Rail... what a waste of timber and time.

唉……雪意飘零，知音何处？那扭曲的舞姿，真想再见一次啊……: (sighs) Snow drifts down, and I am alone in my admiration. Where has my kindred spirit gone? Oh, to see that wondrous dance just one more time...
唉……青溪有你有孙愿前辈，手札定可物尽其用，而说到事发之地的开封……: Well... with you and Elder Sun Yuan on the Silver Needle's side, those notes will surely be put to good use. But as for Kaifeng, where it all began...
唉……骨头再硬，砍几刀也断了。: Heh... even the hardest bones break under the blade.
唉。我与他一同长大，我知道，眼前种种，并非他的本心。: **Sighs** I grew up with him, so I know this isn't what he intended.
唉。我给他们烧炷香吧。哥几个早点走，下辈子投个好胎，过好日子。殿里我记得就有香。: Yeah. Let me light some incense for them. Safe travels, brothers. Better luck next time around. There should be some in the main hall.
唉不就是和圆圆决裂么，这有啥啊。: All this drama over breaking up with Yuanyuan. What's the big deal?

唉呀，知道嘛……贾奶奶和潘大叔，肯定又跟个老学究一样，对着我劈里啪啦讲个没完。: You just know Granny Jia and Uncle Pan are going to sit me down and lecture me till my ears fall off.
唉哟……头、头儿，我头好晕……那老秃驴，一棍子杵我脑门上了……: Eurgh, my head... that bald old man split my skull open, I swear...
唉唉，记得帮我问啊——: Hey, don't forget to ask that question for me!
唉没办法，我虽是第一次操作飞车，奈何天赋异禀啊！: What can I say, it's my first time on one of these, but natural talent is hard to suppress!
唉要是我能快点长大，能帮姐姐背一点东西就好了……: If only I could grow up faster, maybe I could help carry some of that weight for Sister...
唉远道而来的朋友~一起来躺着晒晒月亮吧~: Yo-ho, friend from afar! Let's bask in the moonlight!

唉！也是……和契丹人比，咱只要钱粮，算仁义了。: Sigh! True enough... I guess. Compared to the Khitan, we only want grain and silver. That's practically mercy.
唉！也罢，那你收好。现在还觉得人家别有用心不？: *sigh* Fine, you keep it. You still think he had bad intentions?
唉！听说是小平的钱不见了，这么多人住一块，也不知道谁偷的……: I heard Xiaoping's money went missing. With so many people packed into one room, who knows who took it...
唉！天寒地冻的，腊酒要得急，还得先校勘一遍方子有没有错。: (Sighs) It's freezing out. They're rushing the winter wine, but we still need to check the recipe.

唉！小爷含着金汤匙出生的时候，哪想过还有今天。: Sigh... When I was born with a silver spoon, I never imagined I would be like this.
唉！就差那么一点点！: Ah, just a hair's breadth away!
唉！怎么又是咱俩？这具太沉了！: Ugh! Why is it always the two of us? This is way too heavy!
唉！我本将心向明月，奈何明月是沟渠……小美先生愚且鲁，不如脱名还故乡。: Sigh... "My heart admires the moon, yet the moon shines only on gutters." Master Little Beauty, dull and rude—better retire to your hometown!

唉！言而总之，你不要去打扰他！解了那毒，他就是个废人，要不解，那破地方，他还得回: Sigh... Just don't bother him, alright? If the poison's cleared, he'll be useless. And if not... he'll have to go back to that awful place!
唉！都是市井之言，我和她打过几个照面，也没见她疯。我若是能扮成女子，也想进去瞧瞧: Well, just gossip. I've met her a few times and never seen her go mad. If I could dress as a woman, I'd love to take a look inside!
唉， 师叔啊，你们倒是出来帮帮我啊……: *Sighs* Uncles, can't any of you come out and lend me a hand?
唉，$T(2005)来得不是时候，刚巧有鱼儿上钩，被你这脚步声吓跑喽。: *sigh* Bad timing, $T(2005). Had a fish on the line, but your steps scared it off.
唉，$T(2014)，下次注意点儿。: Ugh, just be more careful next time.
唉，一会又要上路喽。真不能多歇几天吗？: Back on the road soon. Can't we stay a bit longer?

唉，一时也说不清……诶？等等，你说折中之法？折中之法……折中之法……: I can't explain it right now... Wait, a compromise? Did you say a compromise?
唉，一算起账就头疼……能不能别让我算账……: Ugh, numbers make my head hurt. Can't someone else do this?
唉，不想干活，干活哪有下棋有意思？: (sighs) Work is so dull. Nothing beats a good game of chess.

唉，不管他，那些个事儿，都没趣的很！: Well, forget about him. Those affairs are all so boring!
唉，不能坐以待毙，再喊喊……有没有人——有贼——贼进宝库了——: I can't just sit here... Help! Anyone! There's a thief in the treasury!
唉，不讲不讲，一想到这个事儿我就又开始头疼了。: Please, let's not talk about it. Just mentioning the work makes my head throb again.
唉，不说了，容我先扒碗面。这么香的饸饹面，我感觉自己现在能吃下八碗！: Enough talking—let me dig into this bowl first. With noodles this good, I could easily eat eight bowls!
唉，为何人总求个有用呢？: Why do we always need a reason to exist?
唉，为何总有人想给大夫增加工作量。: Why do people insist on making more work for doctors?
唉，为啥人就不能白天铜钱坊，晚上草鞋坊呢……一人共侍二坊，我可以啊！: Why can't I do Coin during the day and Straw Shoes at night? Split my time, I could handle it!
唉，也不知劳役服完，还能否赶上下一个月圆之夜！: Well, I just hope I finish my sentence in time to catch the next full moon!
唉，也不知这人要站到何时。: How long is this one going to stand there?
唉，也只能在这儿说说了……: **Sighs**... I can only talk about this here, you know?
唉，也好，只是又得麻烦你了。: **Sighs** Guess I'll have to bother you again.
唉，也罢。将来到了黄泉之下，终究还能再聚。到时候再一起喝酒……: Well, when I cross over, we'll meet again. And we'll share another drink.
唉，二三十人，说出来是轻飘飘的，可我位低权微，哪能等来这些人啊！: Twenty or thirty! Easy to say. I can barely get one person to listen to me, let alone thirty.
唉，人之常情啊。易地而处，我说话只会比他更难听。: Well, that's only natural. If I were in his place, I'd probably be even harsher.
唉，人心不古啊……: What has the world come to...
唉，人心不古，人心不古啊。: People aren't what they used to be.
唉，人生在世，还是靠关系走后门的多啊……: *Sighs* It's all about making connections and sneaking in through the back door...

唉，人老了，不经撞。: These old bones can't take a hit like that.
唉，人老了，记性就是不好。: Memory's the first thing to go at my age.
唉，今晚大家伙儿又要勒紧裤腰带了。: Well, looks like we'll all have to tighten our belts again tonight.

唉，以前老是夜里接活，如今闲了，怎么还越夜越精神……: Alas... I used to work late into the night, but now that I'm retired, I seem to get livelier as the night goes on...

唉，但凡有口饭吃，谁愿如此。: If I had any other choice, you think I'd be doing this?

唉，这个月又没找到几个枣儿……: Sigh, hardly got any jujubes this month...
唉，这么说来，我真是有些汗颜。: Well, when you put it like that, I'm really ashamed of myself.
唉，这事儿吧……虽然小$T(2007)你这忙帮得不咋地，但也是为俺奔波了一气儿，: Sigh... Well, you did help, $T(2007), even if it wasn't much. The Well of Heaven can't let effort go unrewarded.
唉，这些地黄只能留着大伙儿自家用了，毕竟不管怎么着也不能坏了咱村药材的好名头！: I guess we'll keep these for ourselves. We can't risk harming the village's reputation.
唉，这位游侠，可否请你去这附近找找田老三，问问他是否了解些什么？: Wanderer, would you speak with Tian Laosan and find out what he knows?
唉，这几个小雪人，便当是那些个小姑娘来过的记号吧……: These little snowmen... I suppose they're all that's left to show those girls were ever here...
唉，这可如何是好……: What am I supposed to do now?
唉，这可是你先开始的啊——让你当，让你当。: (sighs) Fine, you started this. You're the boss.
唉，这啥时能掏干净啊……: Sigh... When will this dredging end...?
唉，这四少，真是无法无天，无法无天！: These Four Young Masters are completely lawless! Lawless!
唉，这坊间岁月无趣，能起点波澜，我自是喜闻乐见的。: Life in the district is boring. I'm always happy to see some excitement.
唉，这城里真是越来越乱了。: This city's getting worse by the day.
唉，这小子，可千万别再瞎参和，招人恨了……: I really hope that kid doesn't get himself into more trouble...
唉，这就叫神仙打架，凡人遭殃。钟楼被毁之后，便无人来修缮吗？: *sigh* Immortals fight, mortals suffer. After the tower was destroyed, no one came to repair it?
唉，这就是所谓的游侠行径？: So this is what wanderers do?
唉，这屋子啊，是陈老爷从前和梨花先生一同饮酒的地儿。: Sigh... Lord Chen used to drink with Master Pear Blossom in this room.
唉，这张图又骗了你多少银两？: How much silver did this map cost you?
唉，这戏本子也还算凑活。: (sighs) Well, the script turned out passable, at least.
唉，这把手气不行，一张大牌也没有……我堂堂九流门长老，从不骗人。: Ugh, my luck's cold this round, not one decent card... But as the Nine Mortal Ways Elder, I never cheat.
唉，这把老骨头不中用了。: These old bones are useless now.
唉，这日子可怎么过。: How am I supposed to live like this?
唉，这是人也吓到了，猴也吓到了……: Scared the people and the monkeys both...
唉，这是四少的地盘，四少发令，小的只有听的份啊……: This is Four Young Masters territory. When they give orders, I can only obey...
唉，这村里待着也没意思，哪里比得上我们幽州……: Well, there's just not much excitement in this village. It's nothing like Youzhou...
唉，这样下去又能拖多久呢？: How much longer can things go on like this?
唉，这般行路，委实危险。: Traveling like that is asking for trouble.
唉，这船，以前可只载过洛神……算了，你要试就试吧，我先去那头等你。: This boat used to carry a goddess... Ah, go ahead and try it. I'll wait for you over there.
唉，这街头巷尾的，从不缺新闻。: Never a dull moment around here.
唉，这都两年了，不都说道主能打的很吗，怎么还不来救我们……: Sigh... It's been two years. Isn't Dao Lord supposed to be a mighty warrior? Why hasn't he come to rescue us?
唉，连孤云弟子都搞不定，不试了不试了。: *sigh* Can't even beat a Lone Cloud disciple... Might as well give up.
唉，那些个将军王爷打仗，连累的却是我们这些小老百姓……: Those generals start wars, and we're the ones who suffer...
唉，那你干嘛又跑回这出过事的坏地方呀。: Then why are you back at where bad things happened?
唉，那儿吹得风也忒凶了……来额们村避风沙的人愈来愈多哩。虽然村里变热闹了，额却总: *Sigh* The wind there is so fierce... More and more people are coming to our village to escape the sandstorms. Although it's livened things up, I'm still a little worried...
唉，那慧药本是佛子座下首徒，按理说应当比贫僧更多受佛子教诲，也不知他究竟是如何想: Sigh... Huiyao was the chief disciple of the Enlightened One, who should have received more teachings than I. How could he commit such misdeeds?
唉，那我这么多小鱼干，只好给其他猫吃咯。: Fine then. Guess I'll give all this fish to the other cats.
唉，那看来书上记载的烈阳掌线索多半也是骗人的了。: I suppose that means the book's information about the Blazing Sun Palm technique is also worthless.
唉，那都是哪年的光景了。: Ugh, that was a long time ago.
唉，那闺女可招人喜欢了，太可惜了。她若是活着，如今也该和你一般年纪。: Sigh, that girl was such a sweetheart. What a shame. If she were still alive, she would be about your age now.
唉，郝五那小甥儿，虽然一向不大聪明，却也称得上纯孝……竟然学会偷家里东西了！: That nephew of hers, Hao Youxian... never the sharpest, but always such a devoted child. And now he's stealing from his own family!
唉，都怪我……本来狗儿生辰，我在狄家定了一壶千日醉来庆祝。: This is all my fault. I ordered a jug of Thousand Day Drunk from the Di family for Gou'er's birthday.
唉，都说文津馆弟子才高八斗、学富五车，这四个呆瓜却比他们师叔那个倒霉蛋还笨上几分: Sigh... they say the disciples of the Inkbound Order are all talented, but those four idiots are even worse than their unlucky senior, Fang Bai.
唉，都说这屋子闹鬼，晚上还有鬼哭一样的风声……本官是真后悔，怪不得好好的客栈三年: They say the place is haunted... and the wind sounds like ghostly wailing. No wonder the inn was suddenly abandoned three years ago. Why didn't I think of that?
唉，门内家丑，少侠切莫见笑。: Let's keep this just between us... I only ask you not to look down on us for it.
唉，门里的长老都说我哭得假，没章法，可我从前在村里也是数一数二的哭灵人。: The elders say I cry like a fake. But I was the best mourner in my village.
唉，闲得我都快发霉了！上回殿门大开……是前年正月，百官朝贺那次？: I'm going stale standing here! When was the last time those gates even opened... the New Year audience two years back?
唉，陈发财，陈发财不见三天了！: (sigh) Where is Chen Facai? He's been missing for three days!
唉，陈大哥若走了，日后遇上事儿，该找谁商量呢……: *Sighs* Who am I supposed to go to for advice after Brother Chen leaves?
唉，陈大哥要找的那酒，到底是什么，竟然价值千金？: Man, what's that wine Brother Chen's after, anyway? I hear it's worth a small fortune.
唉，陈大哥这么好的人，都被四少逼走了……: Brother Chen is such a good guy, and even he got run off by Fourth Young Master...
唉，陈娘子啊，你要如何才能明白我的心意呢？: Ah, Mrs. Chen, how can I make you truly understand my heart?
唉，非要打一架才行吗？: Do we really have to fight?
唉，非要走到这一步吗？: Did it have to come to this?
唉，骗来骗去的，什么时候是个头呢……: We just keep conning people over and over... When does it end?
唉，鱼在网中，人何尝不也是呢……: A fish caught in my net... And here I am, in a net that I can't get out of...
唉，齐师弟最擅记路，要是此时此刻他在这里该有多好哇……: Qi has a head for directions. Wish he were here now.
唐·元稹\n\n#Y侠客不怕死，怕在事不成。#E\n事成不肯藏姓名，我非窃贼谁夜:
Yuan Zhen, Tang Dynasty 

#YThe hero fears not death's embrace,
But dreams undone and lost in disgrace. #E
When triumph shines, no need to hide,
I'm no thief who stalks by night's side. 

By daylight's gleam, with honor's hand,
Yuan Ang falls by the justice's stand.
Through Chang'an streets, pale faces spread—
A quiet fear in whispers said. 
This heart, like a whale that cleaves the sea,
Parts raging waves relentlessly. 

With cunning deep, beyond all sight,
A hero's blade decides the fight.
A three-foot sword, a serpent's sway,
Can turn the course of realms one day.
唐·刘沧\n\n经过此地无穷事，一望凄然感废兴。\n渭水故都秦二世，咸原秋草汉诸:
Liu Cang, Tang Dynasty 

Endless histories haunt this place;
Desolate vistas speak of rise and fall. 
The Wei River saw Qin's brief reign,
Autumn grass shrouds Han tombs on the plain. 

#YWild geese cry past frontier skies,
Lone village lamps through bare trees rise.#E 
How much regret in this vast view?
Cold peaks half-veiled in clouds look new.

#YThough the washing and sifting are painstaking,

Chang Jian, Tang Dynasty 

At dawn, I stroll through halls of age-old stone,
Sunlight gilds treetops, golden and alone. 
Winding paths lead where silence softly grows,
Among the blooms where a tranquil spirit flows. 

Birds in flight sing free, the mountain's grace,
The pond reflects a calm and peaceful face. 
#YAll life slips quietly in the morning's glow,
Save for the bells that sing both soft and low.#E

Yet greet many with grace and head bowed.

White-haired and mourning, time won't heal.
In aged years, my tears flow free,

#YThrough withered fields and villages bare,
A year of toil leads nowhere there. #E
At dawn, the reeds reach to the sky,
While crickets chant their mournful cry. 

Home lies beyond the Huai's wide stream,
Friends scattered far like a distant dream. 
Alone, my boat drifts cold and gray,
As Shouyang fades and rivers sway.

Xiang Si, Tang Dynasty

A stream divides to each domain. #E

Fresh deer tracks mark the grassy way. 

Tea fragrance curls from thatched‑roof eaves,
Silk reels hum through the bamboo leaves. 
A herb‑man laughs along the road:
"Care to join me where clouds unload?"

唐代诗人白居易诗作。系《新乐府》第二十首。该诗刻画了一名冒死从异族强占的陇右地区: A poem by the Tang Dynasty poet Bai Juyi. It is the twentieth poem in his New Music Bureau series. Yuan Zhen also has a poem of the same title.

唐宫织物绮丽繁复，裁作羽衣似真似幻。\n若着上旧日繁华，忘却己身是客，便能醉眼看:
Imperial Tang fabrics weave intricate patterns, crafted into feathered robes that blur reality and fantasy.
When draped in bygone luxury, you may forget you are but a mere visitor—gazing through intoxicated eyes at jeweled steeds, scented carriages, and peach blossoms thick with dew.
Yet all fades: a night of swaying crimson, a month of spring breeze... a river flowing ever eastward.

In the late Tang Dynasty, in Yucheng of Jiangnan, stood Udumbara Temple, famed for its Pill Spring Well. A monk named Shanshi lived there alone. 
As wars ravaged the land, a wounded white deer sought refuge in the temple. Shanshi healed its wounds, and the deer lingered, unwilling to leave. 
Over a decade later, during a worship ceremony, villagers caught sight of a deer tomb behind Shanshi's quarters—and beside it, a graceful maiden calling herself the Deer Maiden. Enraged, they slapped Shanshi for desecrating the holy site and planned to sell the maiden. As Shanshi wept helplessly, no amount of pleading could stop them. 
The Deer Maiden wiped Shanshi's tears, clasped her hands, and said: "I shall be the mother of immortality." Then she leaped into the well. 
Colored clouds surged from the well, lifting her to the sky. The villagers hailed her as an immortal and departed in awe. That night, Shanshi passed away in meditation by the well.

#Y$SN#E, just wait until my "vacation" is over. Once I've enjoyed myself enough, I'll definitely come home with the money in glory!

嘿嘿，准备好成为群英会上的贵宾了吗？: Heh heh, ready to be the honored guest of the Heroes Assembly?
嘿嘿，刚刚过来，这里发生什么了: Just got here. What did I miss?
嘿嘿，到手了！希望能帮我拿个好名次~: Got it! I'm definitely placing top three with this.
嘿嘿，到手咯，撤退撤退。: Got it. Time to get out of here.
嘿嘿，加上你和我，目前整整两个人。到时候我负责留声匣，我们的大社长还有更重要的任: Hehe. Counting you and me... two strong. I'll work the Voice Box. You, our Guild Leader, have got the real job...
嘿嘿，只要把弄死各位，这屋里的东西便都归我了！: Hehe, as long as I kill all of you, everything in this room will be mine!
嘿嘿，只要运到这儿来，价钱保管翻倍，怎么卖都是赚！怎样，要不要和我跑一趟？: Get it here, double the price. Easy money. So, you want in?
嘿嘿，可不是，今儿晚上又抓了一个。: Hehe, you bet. We caught another one tonight.
嘿嘿，吓到你啦！怎样，我装得像吧？: (laughs) Got you! Pretty convincing, wasn't I?
嘿嘿，咱也不以大欺小，便先让你一杯又何妨！: Hehe, I won't bully a child. I'll even give you a one-cup head start!
嘿嘿，咱俩联手，那必然三个脑壳顶一个墨家巨子！: Heh, put the two of us together and we've got three heads, which is at least one more than a Grandmaster!
嘿嘿，嘿嘿~你抓不住我！: Hehe! Hehe! You won't catch me!
嘿嘿，夏妹妹坐稳了，我要推喽！: Alright, hold on tight. Here comes the push!
嘿嘿，大人，天下没有免费的美酒呐！: Heh heh, no free wine in this world, Master!
嘿嘿，大侠你知道不？这主意还是我家易儿出的哩。: Hehe. Know what, hero? This was Yi'er's idea.
嘿嘿，天叔，最近又忙什么去了，好久不见你，是不是你和寒姨……: Heh, Uncle Tian, where have you been lately? Haven't seen you in forever... or is it because you and Aunt Han are up to something?
嘿嘿，奶奶是给小月鹿抓来星星了！又大又圆的白玉盘……可漂亮了……: Hehe, I've come to bring you the stars, Xiao Yuelu. And that big, round moon… it's so beautiful.
嘿嘿，好嘞！您稍等！我这就开始张罗人！: Hehe, okay! Please wait a moment! I'll start getting people together right away!
嘿嘿，姓胡的，磨磨蹭蹭的，还不喝干嘛呢？: Hey, why so hesitant? What's stopping you from drinking?
嘿嘿，客官，下次若还想知道这坊间的消息，尽管来找小的！: Heh, friend, if you want to keep up with the local gossip, just come find me anytime!
嘿嘿，寒姨，我突然想起岑夫子教我们的新诗！: Oh! Aunt Han, I just remembered the new poem Cen Fuzi taught us.
嘿嘿，对少侠而言，定是轻而易举的小事！: Heh, this should be a breeze for someone like you!
嘿嘿，小人对这里熟着呢……: Hehe, I know these alleys like the lines on my palm...
嘿嘿，小娘子，此一时彼一时，现今可不是那妙善禅师在的时候啦，他都不在了，我们兄弟: Hey miss, there's no time to lose. Master Miaoshan is no longer here, so we have nothing to be scared of.
嘿嘿，小阮还爱捉迷藏，藏到了水眼里，等你，等你找她。: *chuckles* Xiaoruan still loves hide and seek. She hid in the drain. She thinks you'd find her.
嘿嘿，少东家，你怎么说话的，咱这可是做的正经买卖！: Haha, Young Master, what are you saying? This is honest business!
嘿嘿，就放床底下，放自己眼皮子底下才安心。等攒够了钱，咱俩出去买好酒喝！: Under my own bed, where else? I sleep better when I can feel it beneath me. Once we've saved enough, you and I are going out for the good stuff!
嘿嘿，当然大封赏。加官进爵，封妻荫子的大封赏。: Hehe, big rewards coming. Promotions, titles, and honors for our families.
嘿嘿，往天上看，看到哪里的宝盒没，你只要帮我把宝盒拿来，价钱么，都好说。: Hehe, look toward the sky. Do you see that treasure box over there? Just help me get it, we can talk about the price.
嘿嘿，心里头乐意，身上就不觉着冷！: When I'm happy on the inside, the cold doesn't bother me!
嘿嘿，怕我下山的时候老头回不来，给他留点惊喜！怎么样，咱这文采，这刀法，还可以吧: In case the old man isn't back before I leave, I wanted to give him something to remember me by! Not bad for a bandit's blade, eh?
嘿嘿，您看——我跑了，可我活下来了。: See? I ran away, and I'm still here.
嘿嘿，您看，这本《池锦集》的第一页我刚刚收集满！: Hehe, look! I've gathered the first page of the Gilt-Fin Collection!
嘿嘿，您这轻功若是不传于世，岂不可惜？: Heh, wouldn't it be a shame if your skill were lost to the world?
嘿嘿，惊喜提前说出口就不惊喜了。待您帮我去这几个地方请回诸位师兄妹，自然见分晓。: If I told you now, it wouldn't be a surprise, would it? Just gather the others from those locations, and you'll see.
嘿嘿，想抓我可没那么容易。不过，我们倒是可以比一比酒，只要你能喝过我，我就跟你走: Hehe, catching me won't be so easy. However, we could have a drinking contest. If you can outdrink me, I'll go with you.
嘿嘿，我也觉得，这出戏若是能成，一定很棒！: Hehe, I think so too. If this play comes together, it'll really be great!
嘿嘿，我们不怕英雄反悔，若是你不答应我们……: Heh, we're not worried you'll back out. If you turn us down, however...
嘿嘿，我们用老师教的匠艺，做了一个机关人偶。: We used what you taught us.
嘿嘿，我先尝一口……: Hehe, let me taste it first...
嘿嘿，我就是想，万一他其实没取到，我就来偷……啊不，保管一下这宝贝，也算，报答旧: Hehe... I was thinking, if he didn't get it, I'd steal it myself, I mean, keep it safe. That would count as repaying the old lord's debt.
嘿嘿，我就知道你是好人！我这不是有备无患嘛！: Hehe, I knew you were a good person! It just pays to be prepared for anything!
嘿嘿，我就知道这里的信息比谷口茶馆的还有意思！: I knew it! Better gossip here than anything at the teahouse!
嘿嘿，我得送小小八去打更了，先走一步，游侠，下次再一起玩啊！: I'd better get Little Xiaoba back to its post. See you next time!
嘿嘿，我是答应老头不让山中任何人知晓，可是游侠你是山外人啊。这可不算违背诺言。所: I promised him. But you're from outside the mountain... that doesn't break my word. Please, wanderer, help me!
嘿嘿，我是解忧司秦奋的弟弟，我叫秦枫！: I'm Qin Feng, Qin Fen's little brother from the Bureau of Relief!
嘿嘿，我有两个，你一个嘛……一个脑壳也很正常，无需自卑。: Well, I've got two heads between me and the noggin. You've only got one, but that's perfectly normal. No need to feel bad about it.
嘿嘿，我武艺最好，将来要效古墨侠者之风，行走四方，锄强扶弱！侠道不熄，天下可平！: Heh heh, My martial arts skills are unmatched! I'm going to be like the ancient Mohist heroes, traveling the world, helping the weak and punishing the wicked! Chivalry endures; peace endures!
My martial arts skills are unmatched! I'm going to be like the ancient Mohist heroes, traveling the world, helping the weak and punishing the wicked! Chivalry endures. Peace endures!
嘿嘿，我现下手上功夫不行，嘴上功夫好，自然要扬长避短了。: Look, my fists aren't much, but my mouth's sharp as a blade. Play to your strengths, right?
嘿嘿，我现在靠我吃到的一手小道消息，来和别人的交换，只换不卖。: Heh, now I swap, not sell, the exclusive insider info I collect.
嘿嘿，我的小金库又多了一笔！阿姐肯定想不到我会把钱藏在哪。柜子？太普通。枕头？没: My secret stash has grown again! Sis will never guess where I've hidden it this time. Cabinets? Boring. Pillows? Cliché. Shoe soles? Smelly. Seems like I'm running out of corners...
嘿嘿，我的朋友，我的汉话你知道，像风沙里面的兔子——跳来跳去找不到嘞！: Hehe, my friend, you know my Han dialect. It's like a rabbit in a sandstorm—jumping around and disappearing!
嘿嘿，我看英雄身手不凡，一身武艺不知胜过几多好汉！: Heh, I can tell you have real skills. You've probably taken down more than your fair share of foes!
嘿嘿，我这里倒是有一段#Y红缨#E，兴许可以大赚一笔呢。: Funny thing, I happen to have a piece of #Yred tassel#E right here. Might be worth something.
嘿嘿，打工有什么不好？只要劳动，就有饭吃。: Heh, what's wrong with working? You always get food on the table as long as you work.
嘿嘿，掌事的和主事的，一字之差，可是天差地别。: Hehe, steward and manager might sound like similar roles, but they're worlds apart.
嘿嘿，搜搜他的身，看看有什么值钱的物事！: Heh, check his pockets and see if he's got anything worth taking!
嘿嘿，明白了吧，可别往外说啊！: Now you understand, right? Just don't tell anyone.
嘿嘿，是黑衣的仙女儿！瞧见那金明池没，夜半三更的时候，总有一个苗条的仙女儿“唰”: Nah, it was that mysterious woman in black! Haven't you seen her at Jinming Pool? Every night at midnight, this beautiful, graceful lady just appears out of nowhere.
嘿嘿，有你们在心里踏实多了，这里可真黑啊……: (nervous laugh) I feel so much better with you lot here. It really is pitch dark...
嘿嘿，有恩人这身手，我就不趟这浑水了！: Heh, with a hero like you around, I'll keep out of it!
嘿嘿，有观音姐姐陪着四处逛，我呢，就忍不住想多兜两圈。: Heh, with you right behind me, how could I not run a little farther?
嘿嘿，朝廷为了兴建百工坊，从川蜀地区迁来不少工匠，这不是跟风赚点钱嘛！: Hehe, the court has moved many craftsmen from the Sichuan region to build the Imperial Artisan Court. I'm just hopping on the trend to make some money!
嘿嘿，本武林至尊行走江湖，可不能丢了面子！: Hehe, as a supreme martial artist of the jianghu, I've got a reputation to uphold!
嘿嘿，果然瞒不过游侠。来，吃几颗梨膏糖吧，甜。: Hehe... seems I can't fool you after all. Here, have some pear candy. It's quite sweet.
嘿嘿，梨花很漂亮吧，是我家寒姨种的。: Hehe, aren't the pear blossoms beautiful? My Aunt Han planted them.
嘿嘿，没写错。你有所不知，我们祁家与马为伴，祖宗传下来的都是驯马养马之术，自然是: Hehe, it's not a mistake. You see, our Qi family has bred horses for generations—our ancestral knowledge is all about taming and raising horses. Naturally it's "Horse Rules."
嘿嘿，没错，她一定还活着。她欠我的还没有还呢，怎么能死？怎么可以死！: Heh… she must be alive. She hasn't repaid what she owes. She can't die! She just can't!
嘿嘿，游侠是在说我吗？: Hehe, wanderer, are you talking about me?
嘿嘿，现在小年轻警惕性可真高！好事！好事啊！: Hehe, youngsters these days are really cautious! Good! That's a good thing!
嘿嘿，皇帝那么多财宝，少一点点，不会被发现啦。: The Emperor has so much treasure. He'd never miss a tiny bit.
嘿嘿，看少东家这话说的，我这么优秀的商人，四塞八荒那可都是我的生意场！: Hehe, you know me. A merchant of my caliber can sell anywhere under the sun!
嘿嘿，真不愧是分水机关，好强的动力！: Heh, look at that. This diversion complex's got some serious power behind it!
嘿嘿，瞒不过$T(2001)，等打开匣子，宝贝我们五五分！: Can't fool you. Once we crack this open, we'll split the loot fifty-fifty!
嘿嘿，瞒不过周叔。是广胡子的商队，他们等会一起回来。: Hehe, nothing gets by you. She's with Beard Guang's caravan. They'll be here soon.
嘿嘿，知我者，夫子也。学生这就去背书，这就去……: Hehe, nobody knows me better than you! I'll go study my books right now...
嘿嘿，知道为啥禁书永远禁不完吗？因为人啊，越不让记，心里记得越牢！: Hehe, do you know why no book can ever be truly banned? Because the more you forbid people to remember, the clearer it stays in their minds!
嘿嘿，离人一饮，不羡神仙。\n听我哥说，要喝这离人泪，就必得来这不羡仙客栈。\n:
Hey—one sip of Parting Tears, and even immortals are forgotten. 
My brother says if you want to taste this Parting Tears, you must come to the Blissful Retreat Inn. 
Only here can you drink the original brew made by Founder Madam Han, the inventor of Parting Tears. 
Each year when Parting Tears is uncorked, a grand Feast Opening Ceremony is held, where the first sip from the opening jar is always a highlight! 
Speaking of which, where did my brother go? That archaeology enthusiast is probably off studying... 
Oh right, the legend of Heaven's Pier's Nine-Twist Stone Boat and the Water Lady! 
Never mind that—let me taste this Parting Tears for him first.
嘿嘿，给我两捆紫茎蓍草，不然我就告诉门主你把他卖了。: Hehe, give me two bundles of violet-stem yarrow, or I'll tell the clan master you snitched on him.
嘿嘿，老哥哥我见过，就在昨日，我打汴梁过来，遇见了南边唐国的使者来求取佛经的车架: Hehe, I have! Just yesterday, on my way from Kaifeng, I encountered the Tang envoys coming to request Buddhist scriptures.
嘿嘿，老大都知道，所谓英雄配美人，就像我和香团儿……: Everybody knows—beauty and hero, just like me and Xiang Tuan'er...
嘿嘿，老大，你瞧好了，我投壶可准了！下次咱俩比比，肯定不输你！: Heh heh! Look how good I am at pitch pot! Let's have a match next time! I'll definitely beat you!
嘿嘿，老板，这是我打的鸡。: Heh, boss, here's the pheasant I caught.
嘿嘿，老金的鼻子可不比那姓万的老头差。只要是钱，就一定逃不出老金的鼻子。: My nose is every bit as sharp as old Wan's. Money has a scent, and I never miss it.
嘿嘿，肚子也舒坦了，话也唠完了，俺也得去找俺兄弟了。让我想想师父是怎么教的来着…: Hehe, my stomach feels better, our chat's done, and I need to find my brethren. Lemme think how my master taught me to say goodbye... Oh yeah! May your feet always find green hills and clear waters!
嘿嘿，肯定是被传言吓破了胆呗。听说三年前，有个#N契丹豪客#E打清河这儿过，要去: Hehe, must've been scared off by the rumors. I heard three years ago that a #NKhitan warrior#E passed through Qinghe heading to the Tang. He stayed at our inn.
嘿嘿，自从搬来这里，我听花笙讲了好多好多你的故事！: Heh, I've heard tales of your exploits since I arrived here. Hua Sheng's kept me up to the chin in stories!
嘿嘿，船大哥，你不去凑个热闹？: Hey, Boatman, aren't you going to join the fun?
嘿嘿，药效还需药药的药匣来，不然只是寻常服用补药，哪能有十分效果？: Hehe, the medicine needs my medicine chest to work properly. Otherwise, how could it be fully effective?
嘿嘿，萍儿姐姐吗，要不是这位大侠帮我，我……我就又要迟到了……: Hehe, is that Ping'er? If not for this great hero's help, I'd have been late again...
嘿嘿，虽然有水汽遮掩，可依然逃不过万某得鼻子，我闻到了温家的火药的味道。: Heh. Water can't fool my nose. I smell Wen family explosive powder.
嘿嘿，要我说，在乐于助人这方面，少东家你从来都是没得说，爽快！: Hehe, when it comes to helping others, you never hesitate. That's so generous!
嘿嘿，让大人见笑了。在这宫里头嘛，脑子不转得快些，累死也落不着好。: Heh. In this palace, if your wits don't move faster than your feet, hard work alone won't save you.
嘿嘿，讲究多着呢，你瞧那侍女没，待那侍女从水中取出离人泪来，放到那水中的小船上。: Oh, definitely! See that maid over there? She takes Parting Tears from the water and puts it on a little boat.
嘿嘿，论神仙渡的蹴鞠大王，还得是我！: Heh, when it comes to Cuju at Heaven's Pier, nobody beats me!
嘿嘿，读不读书和是不是万事知也没关系嘛。: Hehe, one doesn't need to read books to be a know-it-all.
嘿嘿，谁让你这么不惜命的？你自己说说，为了那载人天灯，这个月你都摔了几次？没有七: Well, whose fault is that? Tell me, how many times have you fallen out of the sky this month over that lantern of yours? Seven? Eight?
嘿嘿，谢大爷小姐的赏。花钱过手，万事亨通。花钱过手，万事亨通。: Hehe, thanks so much for the reward. When Charm changes hands, everything falls into place. Everything falls into place!
嘿嘿，谢谢少侠！事成之后，咱就在这儿汇合！: Thanks! When it's done, we'll meet back here!
嘿嘿，走、走！不过我可不是瞎说，雪怪这事大伙儿都这么传呢。: Haha, come on! But I'm not making it up. The snow monster rumors are everywhere.
嘿嘿，赵小姐……进了我怜花禅院的门，就是我禅院的人了。你蒙着面纱也太见外了，来来: Heh... Lady Zhao. You walked through the gates of Bloomveil Monastery and now you're one of us. No need for the veil, sweetheart. Come, let big brother take it off for you.
嘿嘿，还不是因为少东家您，身份贵重……那自然大伙都想引你注意，$T(5074)！: Well, you're the young master. Of course everyone wants your attention. Go ahead! Marry into that wealthy family!
嘿嘿，还得是咱们老大高明，骗那些贱骨头这是佛花。现如今可不是服服帖帖的？: Hehe, yeah. Clever! You tricked those worthless bones. They think these are buddha flowers. Now they're all obedient.
嘿嘿，还得是游侠你有手段。: Heh, gotta hand it to you, you really know how to hold your own.
嘿嘿，还是少侠你懂我！: Heh, only you really get me, Young Hero!
嘿嘿，还是老兄算术好。九百九十九个不行，那就九千九百九十九个！: Haha, your math is good! If 999 won't do, then let's shoot for 9,999!
嘿嘿，还有更妙的——: And wait till you hear the best part...
嘿嘿，这#Y红缨#E我只卖给#Y磐老太#E，其他人想都别想。: Hehe, I'm only selling this #Yred tassel#E to #YGranny Pan#E. No one else.
嘿嘿，这……借你吉言，希望你的话本子也能名动天下！: Hah, I appreciate it. I hope your stories are known across the realm as well!
嘿嘿，这不刚刚给张家食肆送完货嘛，来喝口茶。: Heh, I was just delivering some groceries to Zhang's Eatery and stopped here for a bit of tea.
嘿嘿，这不感谢你帮额找马嘛！二马，咱们走……: Hehe, it's thanks for helping me find Er Ma! Er Ma. Let's go...
嘿嘿，这不是习惯了嘛，以前总想着法子见她，现在快成婚了。不知为何，反而更想一直陪: Hehe, it's just become a habit. I was always thinking of ways to see her. Now that we're about to get married, I somehow feel more eager to be with her all the time.
嘿嘿，这不是还有您这样的好大夫吗？还不要钱呢……您真是大圣人！: Heh, but that's what makes having a great doctor like you so lucky! You even patch me up for free... You're a real lifesaver!
嘿嘿，这个嘛，是同外人的说辞！天尊既发话，那施主自然不是外人了！: Heh heh, that's just what we tell outsiders. Since the heavens have spoken, you're no outsider anymore!
嘿嘿，这可不是我偷拿，是珍儿心疼我，非要给我的。: Hehe, I didn't steal this. Zhen'er insisted I take it.
嘿嘿，这可是咱们攒了半个月的‘金汁’，倒进河里让他们喝个够！: Heh, this is the "liquid gold" we've collected over half a month. We'll pour it into the river and let them have their fill.
嘿嘿，这可是我好不容易抓到的，不用跟我客气！: Here, take it. Caught it myself.
嘿嘿，这回咱们可是火速赶来的，还成吧？: Heh heh, we rushed here as fast as we could. How's that?
嘿嘿，这坊子啊就是俺家，有得休，俺就满足哩！老板还给俺发了烟花呢！: This is already my home! Having time to rest is enough for me! My boss even gave me fireworks!
嘿嘿，这就靠你自己琢磨了。: Heh... that's for you to figure out yourself.
嘿嘿，这接下来的消息可就要钱了。当然游侠要是没钱，咱这里倒是有桩生意，就是不知道: The rest'll cost you. Unless you'd rather do a job for me instead.
嘿嘿，这故事啊，就像那酒楼的美酒，不得花点儿小钱，才能尝上一口？: Heh heh, a good story is like fine wine. Takes a coin or two to get a taste, wouldn't you say?

They are one of the unique forms of ancient Chinese maps, later renamed local chronicles. The earliest extant tujing, discovered in the Dunhuang Library Cave, is the Illustrated Treatise of the Shazhou Protectorate. Compiled during the High Tang period, it records the geography, history, and customs of Tang-era Shazhou and its subordinate counties, Dunhuang and Shouchang, comprising 667 lines.

在凉州这个地界，若问起安琉璃是什么人，可能没几个人知道。但要说到把戏团的神仙索，:
In the land of Liangzhou, if you ask who An Liuli is, few people might know. But if you mention the "Immortal Rope" from the acrobatic troupe, everyone will let out a knowing "Oh".  
The Immortal Rope was one of the troupe's star performers, mainly specializing in high-wire walking. High-wire walking wasn't particularly rare, but with her stunning looks, sweet words, agile skills, and vague rumors of "possessing supernatural powers," it was only natural that she was beloved by the noble ladies of Liangzhou. However, it would be unfair to call her a playboy. The Immortal Rope was probably still too young to understand love, she had a childlike nature that valued drawing her dagger to face a general more than keeping a date with a beauty. It's not that no women had flirted with her, but such encounters always ended in absurdity.  
So when the Immortal Rope sneaked out again to go to the Cao Manor, Zhuge Ha stopped her.  
"What are you up to?"  
The Immortal Rope's eyes wandered: "Nothing. I'm going out to play."  
Zhuge Ha glanced at the acrobatic props on her back and frowned deeply: "Why are you bringing this stuff?"  
"What else? I'm going to do tricks, of course."  
"Oh" Zhuge Ha nodded meaningfully: "Planning to perform 'plucking the moon from the sky'... What are you really up to?"  
"What do you mean what am I up to..."  
"Hmph, you'd better not be up to anything. Otherwise, this old man won't be polite."  
"You old fart! So boring!"  
The Immortal Rope ran off in a flash.  
Zhuge Ha watched An Liuli skip away. Around her waist was a sturdy red silk ribbon, her old friend, the "Immortal Rope" she used for her signature act.  
People like them had cheap lives, not even noticed by heaven. They were born in obscurity and died silently. A single fall, a bitter cold wind, a run to chase someone they cared about, any of these could be the cause of their death.  
His Liuli was a good child. Now she had stepped onto a shaky high wire, somersaulting joyfully thousands of feet above the ground, treading on thin ice without realizing it. If there really were immortals, Buddhas, or heaven, they should lower a straight Immortal Rope connecting to the sky when this child falls, save her.

在很早很早以前，阿依奴还是一个和葡萄苗差不多高的小姑娘。\n她总爱趁阿爸不注意，:
Long, long ago, Aynur was still a little girl about as tall as a grapevine seedling. 
She loved to sneak to the entrance of the neighbor's vineyard when Father wasn't looking, blink her round eyes, and ask softly, "Auntie... the grapes smell so good... could you give me one to taste?" 
This trick never failed. Aynur always got a big, sweet grape. 
 
But every time Father caught her, she'd get scolded. 
The people around persuaded him: "Ah, what's the harm in losing one grape? Little Aynur beats our shoulders and rubs our legs, we'd even plant two more grapevines just to make her happy!" 
But her father frowned, grapes were the lifeblood of farmer families, not sweet snacks. How could she ask others for them casually? "If you're really craving... can't you eat our own grapes? Are the grapes your father grows not sweet enough?" 
"That's not it!" Aynur would whisper in protest, Father's grapes are the best. But... but Father and Brother guarded the grapevines all night making wine, whenever she saw their grapes, she thought they tasted of sweat, very bitter. 
Hearing this, Father could only sigh helplessly, apologized to everyone, and silently led Aynur back home. 
 
The next day, Aynur rubbed her eyes and pushed open the window to find a small, newly transplanted grapevine by their doorstep! This was a home grapevine planted just for her, not for making wine. 
From then on, Aynur would count the grapes on the vine every night before bed, calculating how many might ripen by morning. If one ripened, she'd eat it herself; if two, she'd share one with Brother; if three... four... then Father, Brother, and Aynur could each have one, and she'd bury one in the soil for Mother! This was a sweetness belonging solely to the family. 

That little grapevine by the doorstep, where did it go later? Later, it was gone.

Many say immortality means an undying body, but I believe true immortality is becoming a legend, living on through countless generations. I follow Master Sun Buqi for that very immortality.

在来到这里之前，她曾以为世界只有黑白两色。\n或是因为在她记忆的最初，还没来得及:
Before coming here, she once believed the world existed only in black and white.
Perhaps it was because, at the very dawn of her memory, the man and woman she never even got to call "Mother" and "Father" had hurriedly stuffed her into a wooden box. They left her to drift along the river's current before they could teach her to recognize any other hues.
Hiding in the pitch darkness, she peeked through a small hole in the wood, watching strange, meteor-like flashes of light darting outside. On a whim, she used her tiny finger to plug the hole, and then released it.
Light, then dark. Light, then dark... To her, it was endlessly fascinating.
The arguing voices of the man and woman faded away; the thunderous roars faded away.
Accompanied only by the tranquil babbling of the water, light and shadow became her entire world.
Oh, world, do you truly possess only these two colors?
It was not until she entered Mohist Hill that she discovered the trees were a lush verdant green; the wind a dusty white; and the springs of the Hidden Mountain ablaze with blooming wildflowers. People, too, were full of vibrant colors.
She learned that the bright lights in the distance were actually the fires of war, while the deepest darkness could serve as a sanctuary.
Fortunately, the little girl of that time did not yet know that twenty years later, she would be the one to change the colors of countless people's destinies.

在记忆中的家乡，每个人都能跳起舞来。\n当姑娘们扬手起舞时，银铃叮当，欢笑不绝—:
In the memories of home, everyone could dance. 
When girls raised their hands, silver bells chimed, laughter unending—a sound that never faded. 
Aynur loved bell bracelets most. With them, she could dance freely, even the dust at her feet sweet like honey. 

Later, she met a princess even more dazzling than the moon. But when the princess walked, the ornaments at her temples swayed with the same pleasant sound as bells—why wasn't the princess happy? 
"These are step-shakers, not free-dancing silver bells." The princess touched the hanging golden tassels. "They remind me of my duty."

Little Aynur didn't understand. She thought: if the princess is unhappy, I'll give her my joyful bells. 
The princess knelt. Gilded step-shakers and silver bells chimed in the wind. "Your joy must stay in your own hands." She returned the bells to Aynur's wrist. She loved the girl's smile and dance, hoping all in Liangzhou could live in peace. 

Young Aynur took the bells and solemnly promised: she would always be happy, never cry.

In the peaceful years before famine struck, the Zheng family of Da'an stood in great prestige. Kind and generous, the Zheng couple earned the respect of all, aiding neighbors and forging goodwill throughout the community.
Then came the birth of young master Zheng E. The whole town rejoiced—guests from far and wide arrived with gifts, the most precious among them a Gilded Longevity Thread handwoven by his grandmother, symbolizing a full life and a wish for a hundred years of peace and joy. Everyone shared that hope.
Those days were warm and bright, filled with harmony and family. It felt as if such happiness would last forever.
But after the chaos of marauders, Zheng E stood alone in the ruins, watching A'Ruan die before his eyes. His home gone, his family lost. Once surrounded by love, now he was the only one left. Reunion? What a cruel joke. Longevity? Only he had lived.
He untied the golden thread, once a symbol of everyone's hopes, and placed it gently on A'Ruan's grave. The one most wished to live long was gone. As for his own life... he left it there too.

在鸿眼中，这世间一切问题都有解，只是需要一点时间而已。\n就像滴水凿石，一点一滴:
To Brant, every riddle in this world had an answer. It was simply a matter of time.
Like water gnawing at stone, drop by drop, year after year, until a hole is finally pierced through. So it was for the Mohist quest for the heavens.
If a century yields no hope, then count by the millennium. Only then can a glimmer of hope be found.
With this realization, Brant had been in the outer sect just over a year.
It felt like a path already paved. In a single glance, he could see the man he would become decades from now.
Studying the intricate flying eagle mechanisms was undeniably fascinating. Yet the deeper he studied, the more those hundred years felt like a single, fleeting breath.
He'd write a few treatises and craft some new mechanisms. Eventually, he'd earn a name and take on a few disciples who might one day walk the path he had envisioned.
He often spoke of dripping water piercing stone, and the humble dew enriching the soil. The logic was sound, yet he felt a lack of... fire.
He could see the future, yet he didn't know how to hold on long enough to reach it.
Must every falling drop carry the exact same glint of hope?
Suddenly, it hit him: the riddles of this world need not have one single solution.
Though many strive toward the same destination, the paths they take are theirs alone to choose.
As the ancients said, "Read thousands of books and travel thousands of miles." He had read enough books. Now the journey lay before him.
Time to take the first step forward.

Karez Well is an ancient underground water conservancy project, mainly distributed in arid regions of China, such as Turpan and Hami in Xinjiang. By digging vertical shafts and constructing underground canals, water evaporation is reduced, allowing meltwater from high mountain glaciers to flow along the terrain into deep desert areas. 
At its peak, there were 1,838 Karez Wells in Xinjiang, with underground canals totaling 5,272 kilometers in length and a maximum annual water output of 610 million cubic meters. Along with the Great Wall and the Grand Canal, it is known as one of the three great ancient engineering projects of China and is also called the "Underwater Great Wall."

Kun the Youngest was a good man. Everyone who had ever received his kindness said so.
Kun the Youngest was also a strange man. And none who had known his kindness would deny that either.
Indeed, Kun the Youngest was both good and strange, but he hadn't been born that way.

Once, he had been a little beggar wandering the land, barely half the size of a grown man and with no skills to speak of. Anyone who took a dislike to him could kick him aside, and he never fought back. Against all odds, he survived, wind-battered, rain-drenched, and along the way, he learned a few tricks to keep himself alive.
For example, powders that made a man itch uncontrollably. Firecrackers that startled pursuers into stumbling. Trinkets others scoffed at, but for him, they were lifelines.

Yet even lifelines sometimes frayed.
When Ni Laoshan first found him, the boy was grievously wounded, blood mingling with rainwater as he curled inside a bamboo basket like a sewer rat.
So Ni Laoshan carried this little rat back to the underground Ghostlight Market, where even vermin could find shelter.

There, Kun the Youngest made his home.
Having known the drenching cold of rain, he always carried compassion. He crafted quirky gadgets and taught others to survive, earning his reputation as "good". 
But the storms of his past ran deep. He hid his true heart behind pranks and laughter, earning the label "strange".

Kun the Youngest was good and strange, because life had left him no other choice.

At a tavern somewhere beyond the frontier, Yi Dao and Chu Qingquan sat perched upon the eaves.
Yi Dao had lost count of his cups, his voice thick and resonant with drink. "Hah! In this one life of ours... what is it that a man should prize above all else?"
He turned to Chu Qingquan. "I'm talking to you!"
"Some prize honor, others prize profit... and then there are those who forsake all else, prizing only a promise kept."
"Spot on! I, the Killerblade, fear nothing in this world, not even death! My only dread is facing my kin in the afterlife and being named a man of broken faith!"
"Rest easy. I shall bear witness. You are a scoundrel, to be sure, but when it comes to honoring a promise, no one does it better."
"Hahahaha! Come, drink!"
"Cease your drinking. If you stir up a storm in your cups, it will be a mess to settle."
"Confound it! Stop nagging. What's my drinking to you?"
"Let us end it here today. I promise you: one day, I shall personally toast you with a jar of the finest Parting Tears."
"One jar?"
"Ten."
"Fine, it's a deal. I'll take your word for it this once!"
Chu Qingquan offered no reply. Slumped against the tiles in a haze of wine, he began to chant something in a low murmur.
Yi Dao couldn't catch the words; he found it a nuisance. With the thirst still burning in his chest, he wobbled to his feet, unsheathed his blade, and danced a drunken dance.
Long after, Yi Dao would realize that what Chu Qingquan had been reciting was an ancient ballad.
"Three cups down, a promise is cast; the Five Great Peaks weigh light at last..." 
"With blurred eyes and ears aglow, a spirit like the white rainbow begins to grow..."
As the final lines of A Warrior's Journey faded, the Killerblade's dance reached its end.

In Mohist City lived a master artisan, devoted to his intricate mechanisms and living a solitary life. One day, he poured his skill into crafting a puppet so lifelike and enchanting that he named her Qiao and called her his wife.
While he was away gathering materials, a lost scholar wandered into the workshop, entranced by Qiao's beauty. The two quietly fell in love and pledged their hearts to one another.
But when the artisan returned and found them together, jealousy consumed him. Enraged to see his "property" stolen, the artisan severed the scholar's head in a single stroke.
Heartbroken, Qiao was weeping. The wind stirred. Her wooden joints splintered; her clockwork heart crumbled to ash. All that remained was a wreckage of heartbreak.

Though many say puppets lack feeling, her love was deeper than life itself.
After Qiao vanished, the artisan lived out his days alone, forever mourning the love he lost.
