It's hard to believe Bai Rong was raised in a noble and strict household.
On the day she came of age, she chose a peach blossom jade pendant to mark the occasion. Peach blossoms have long symbolized romantic feelings, and when her rigid, old-fashioned father saw it, he immediately flew into a rage. Her mother tried to smooth things over with a line from the classics—"A daughter marries, bringing harmony to her new home"—but the headstrong young Bai Rong retorted without hesitation: "Peach blossom waters run clear, where mandarin ducks bathe above."
A storm of scolding and punishment inevitably followed.
But Bai Rong was born delicate and willful, blessed with striking beauty. In a place like that, whether intentional or not, she was often blamed for things beyond her control.
"If you all insist I'm a seductress, wouldn't it be a waste of the name if I knew nothing of love?"
Out of spite, she joined the Velvet Shade Society and severed ties with her so-called family.
Only her mother ever visited her in Kaifeng—years later, by then spring's tender charm had already made countless admirers fall at Bai Rong's feet. Her mother said little and did even less. She simply left behind the peach blossom pendant and a single remark: even stories of two hearts in love and a daughter's return home are not always something to be condemned.
Did Bai Rong understand what her mother meant? Perhaps she'd long forgotten. But she did, after all, leave that same peach blossom pendant on the flower boat the man was sure to board.

West of Jadebrook Mountain lies Mercyheart Town, once called Stonemason Town, where the people made their living by quarrying stone.
During the Kaiyuan era of the Tang Dynasty, the emperor established the Fahua Temple on the town's outskirts, enshrining thousands of Buddhist scriptures. A master sculptor surnamed Yang arrived from afar with his disciples, settling in the town. For years, they journeyed between the quarry and the monastery, studying the sutras, sculpting countless stone figures. Arhats, Guanyin, and bodhisattvas flowed from their chisels, each statue imbued with both exquisite detail and divine spirit. Their work was praised throughout the land, and so Stonemason Town came to be known as Mercyheart Town.
For generations thereafter, the townsfolk made their livelihood through Buddhist sculpture. But in the last dynasty, with Buddhism banned, the craft fell into decline. Now, upon entering Mercyheart Town, one sees only toppled statues buried in wild grass, moss creeping over faces once radiant with sacred grace. The master sculptors are long gone—scattered, forgotten. The quarries are choked with weeds; the carving halls echo with silence.
Only a few dozen villagers remain. Day and night, they move through the town with strange purpose, planting grotesque flowers in every corner. They nourish them with their very flesh. Their presence, their rituals—unnatural. The sight alone chills the blood.

慧这个名字，起得好也不好。\n人说“慧极必伤”，他向来嗤之以鼻。\n公输之姓，匠:
"Hui" means wisdom. It is a name that cuts both ways. 

People always say that too much wisdom brings early ruin, but he scoffed at the notion. Born of the Gongshu bloodline, the true heirs to the artisans' craft, he was admitted to the Inner Sect at the age of twenty and taken in by Elder Peng. Talent, intellect, and a masterful touch, he possessed them all. Where was the ruin in that? He was perfectly worthy of the name Hui. What ruin could there be?

It was deep spring in the mountains, and the Dragonbane Wood was just sprouting fresh leaves. It was his turn to patrol the forest with Chu Ying, a disciple of Elder Crane.
They came across a Dragonbane tree scarred by lightning, which sparked a sudden debate on whether the ultimate pinnacle of mechanics lay in Ingenuity or Simplicity.

"This dead trunk," Chu Ying asked, "if it were yours to fashion into a device, where could the Ingenuity be found?"
"The tree is dead," Gongshu Hui replied flatly. "There is no Ingenuity to be found."
Chu Ying laughed. "No Ingenuity? Just watch."
Saying that, he pushed the dead tree over and buried it beneath the soil. "Come next year, the trees nearby will grow all the better for it."

Gongshu Hui thought to himself that this man was rather clever.
A clever man has no business doing foolish things. 

So when Chu Ying announced he was leaving the mountains to wander the world with Elder Crane, Hui did not say a word to stop him. He only said that if Chu Ying did not return in three years, the largest Dragonbane tree on the cliff would belong to him.

Chu Ying laughed heartily. "Deal! And if I don't come back, you can bury me right under it!"
Gongshu Hui shot him a glance, thinking the remark was utterly foolish.
A clever man would never do foolish things.

When the letter from the Lodestar Swordmaster finally arrived, Gongshu Hui stood staring at the notches carved into the tree, feeling a rare moment of hesitation.
Yet he also knew it was nothing more than a Dragonbane tree.
Besides, withered wood knows no second spring. Only by cutting away the decay can the new sprouts find room to grow.

A clever man never regrets.

我与那位将军做了一笔交易，我为他提供粮食，他为我修造水井。\n即便是长途迁徙的飞:
I struck a deal with the general: I provide the grain, and he builds the well.
Even migrating birds need a place to rest on their long journey. For the Sogdian caravans, these resting places are always found where there is water.
But this time, my stay has been longer than I intended—perhaps because digging a well is a slow and arduous task.
At first, the Tang army sent only a few men. They still had a city to guard, so progress was slow. Just as I'd calculated, it was not a profitable deal.
But then, villagers started to appear. They helped the soldiers, not for coin or for profit. They couldn't quite explain why, only murmuring about wanting to see the Central Plains, to see Chang'an again.
Chang'an. I once longed for that city myself. In the lessons of trade passed down from my elders, it was a land one could only travel to after becoming a great merchant, carrying credentials and chanting prayers.
But what reason did these soldiers and villagers have, most of whom had never even been there?
I asked the general as he stood on the city wall. He told me Chang'an is the heart of their country. Their homeland.
I didn't understand what "homeland" meant. "A homeland," he explained, "is where you have ties. It's the place that lets a wanderer stop wandering."
His meaning still eluded me. "If I go to Chang'an myself," I asked, "will I understand?"
He shook his head. "You would. But you shouldn't go. Not now."
"If I would understand, then I must go." I smiled, countering with a new business proposal. "You've been looking for a foreigner the Bodchen wouldn't suspect, someone to travel light and carry a message to Chang'an. Let me go for you!"
I leaned forward, snatched the whip from his hand, and set off on his white horse, crossing three passes and a thousand miles to reach the fabled city of Chang'an.
It was magnificent. But strangely, I found myself missing the simple market where I'd spent my days with the soldiers and villagers.
When I returned, I saw a small light flickering in the shelter where I had stayed.
The guard at the gate greeted me with a smile. "The general said your return was uncertain, Master Kang, so he ordered us to keep a lamp lit for you."
In that moment, I understood. This is what a homeland is.
Suddenly, I had a new dream: to build this place bigger, better. To let the desert poplars sink their roots here and grow a thousand golden branches.
I want to build my "homeland" into a true home for the Sogdian people.

我乃孤云弟子，今不幸困死此处，留书以助后人。\n第一日，沙场点兵，战的痛快。以为:
I am a disciple of Lone Cloud, trapped here and fated to die. May this writing serve those who follow me into this place.

On the first day, we mustered on the field and fought with valor. I presumed that once the battle was won, we could leave the pass.
But after scores of battles, through both victory and defeat, we found ourselves returned to the place where the war drums sound. It is a loop without end.

I have kept watch. For one day, I stood guard at the supply tower and saw the soldiers move grain fifteen times. The moment I stepped away, they stopped. For another, I sat atop the city tower as arrows rained down without pause. The moment I left, they ceased.
It has been forty-nine days, forty-nine cycles. My attempts to escape have been countless, and all have failed.

This city is a graveyard for hundreds. They were likely martial artists like myself, drawn into this trap. Some left notes, others carvings, but the wind and sand have claimed most of them.

To this day, I have found no answers. I know only this: the secret lies with the Anxi Army, and with Guo Xin.

我们如果把那边的船烧了，熔炉这边的守备肯定会去救火，到时候……: If we set it ablaze, the guards will scramble to put it out—
我们姚大夫，好生厉害啊！辛苦了，这软嫩的柿子送你，就当犒劳了。: Our Doctor Yao is something else! Here, you've earned these. Nice and ripe, the best of the batch.
我们家住在渭阳屯，就在芥子庐西北的地界上。再往前数个几年，大家伙儿还都在凉州挨饿: We're from Weiyang Village, northwest of here. A few years ago, we were starving in Liangzhou. Had to leave our homes and move east.
我们家农场里什么都有，春天有花，秋天有柿子，到了冬天，河边的仙鹤像画一样……: Our farm is beautiful year-round... flowers bloom in spring, persimmons ripen in fall, and in winter, the cranes by the river look like art.
我们家在寿昌坊也算有头有脸的大户人家，别人指不定怎么说闲话呢……: Our family's pretty well-known here in the Prosperity Haven. Who knows what kind of rumors will start flying...
我们家大侠在江湖里可是威风了？: So? Has our wanderer been making a name out there in the jianghu?
我们家家门不幸啊！老沈！你说说，咱两家什么关系？他这当准姑爷的人了，上你家门儿来: What a calamity for our families! Old Shen, look at us. Our families are so close, and he's practically your son-in-law. Is it really such a big deal for him to visit?
我们家小姐一直想要位闺中密友，若因此次经历找到了金兰姐妹，也未可知呢……: Our young lady has always longed for a close friend. Who knows, perhaps this encounter will lead to sworn sisterhood...
我们家小姐还未婚配，若因此次经历找到了乘龙快婿，也未可知呢……: Our young mistress is yet unmarried. Who knows, perhaps this experience will help her find a worthy husband...
我们家族，世世代代近亲通婚，为了守护巫山地底的那座古墓。: My clan had practiced inbreeding for generations to guard an ancient tomb beneath Wushan Mountain.
我们家现在有河边这两块儿，但我可不满足。我要买更大的地，再开个马场……: We already have two plots by the river, but I want more. I'd like to buy a larger piece and open a horse ranch someday...
我们家的蛋比别家的都大，养出来的鸡肉质紧实，每天都能下蛋呢。: Our eggs are bigger than most, and the chickens that hatch from them are strong. They lay eggs every day.
我们家老孙的手啊，稳得很！您就放一百个心！: Old Sun's hands don't shake a bit! You're in good hands!
我们家老爹啊，就好射覆这一口，答不上来，便不准吃饭，哎呀，我和我三哥可不是这块料: Our old man loves his riddles. Can't answer? No food! My third brother and I just aren't cut out for this. If only Shi Xizai were here!
我们家那口子非嫌我懒，让我出门学个手艺……: My woman says I'm lazy. Sent me out to learn a trade...
我们小阿然要替我讨公道了是不是？: Looks like little Ran's going to stand up for me, aren't you?
我们少爷花了大价钱购粮，又低价卖面……即便是家里有金山银山，也经不起这么耗！: Our Young Master spent a fortune buying grain and selling cheap noodles. Even a house full of gold couldn't sustain that for long.
我们就不用太担心了。: So we don't need to worry too much.
我们就在这里等大侠吧！: Let's wait here for the hero!
我们就看着这家小娃娃就从来苏蒙学后头绕个弯，风一样就跑了。: We'd watch this little kid come around from behind Hopewell Academy and run off like the wind.
我们已探得#M君无逸#E和#M太白剑#E的下落，果然不出您所料，真在这雪谷之中！: We've confirmed the whereabouts of #MJun Wuyi#E and the #MTaibai Sword#E—just as you expected, they're hidden deep within Snow Valley. However, the #MSnow Monster#E has been standing in our way. We'll press on and push further into the valley tomorrow.
我们已是有福的了，在众医家的帮助下陆陆续续地搬了家。你看看南边的达安村和隐雾林，: We're already the lucky ones. With help from many doctors, we managed to move houses. Just look at Sorrowfield Village, Mistveil Forest down south, and the Mercy Hall to the east...
我们已经寻得孩子的爹娘，他们会在清玉岸边等他。: We've found his parents. They'll be waiting at the shore.
我们已经相依为命了四十年了……四十年前，我也是流落到这里，大相国寺的一只白鸟救了: We've lived together for forty years. Long ago, I fled here seeking shelter, and it was a white bird from Grand Imperial Temple that saved me.
我们已经跟九流门的兄弟姐妹打好招呼了，和附近住户聊聊，租下空地来办集市。: We've already spoken to the Nine Mortal Ways folk and the nearby households. The open ground is ours for the market.
我们师门，正是为支援王清师叔而来。我脚程快些，就在这镇戍仓多呆了几日。: We came to reinforce Martial Uncle Wang Qing. I move fast, so I lingered at the Toilgrain Barn a few extra days.
我们带出来的东西本就不是最深处的秘宝，就算能换些银子，也经不住这么多人分。: The treasures we brought back aren't even the deepest secrets. Even if we get some silver for them, it's barely enough to split among so many.
我们带出来的东西本就不是最深处的秘宝，能换的银子总不会太多。再不给牺牲的人多分些: The treasures we brought back aren't the deepest secrets, so the payout won't be much. If we don't give the fallen more, how are their families supposed to get by?
我们庄里的祁阿大，在璧泉山找着了夜露飞光！: One of our people found Night Flash at Jadebrook Mountain.
我们张家两代浴血，收复河西，矢志归唐，忠心可昭日月。: The Zhang family bled for two generations to reclaim Hexi. Our loyalty is beyond question.
我们当中有妻儿，有父母，此刻他们在南边还能得享安逸。但若是虏人再往南，整个中原都: We all have families, wives, children, parents, safe in the south for now. But if the enemy pushes further, the entire Central Plains will burn.
我们当时还说着呢，这烈女怕缠郎，这反过来也一样呢。: We always said persistent men wear down stubborn women. Goes both ways, I guess.
我们很高兴地通知同道，您作为共同作者参与的论文经审核符合《织网》要求，决定予以发:
We are pleased to inform you that the paper you co-authored has been accepted by "The Web."
The academic path is solitary and steep, but with fellow travelers, the way feels less lonely.
我们得去帮泉儿哥找叶子！找到#Y不死树的叶子#E，他们家就没事了！: We're helping Liquan find the #YImmortal Leaf#E. If we do, everything will be okay at his house!
我们得快点儿准备，看书授课都是伤脑子的活计，: We've got to prepare quickly—teaching and reading both are quite demanding.
我们得快点儿，主宅就在这边！: We have to hurry! The main house is this way!
我们得悄然接近，探知他们的计划。: We need to get closer and find out what they're planning.
我们得想办法把今日所见传回去，至少不能让你父亲枉死。你活着，家才活着。: We have to get word out about what happened today. Your father's death can't be for nothing. While you live, your family lives.
我们得至少保证让他们都吃上一口热饭！: We have to at least make sure they all are fed!
我们想着，给这市楼准备做点新东西！拆了穆吞的东西，现在这鸱吻还没定下来。: We want to give it a new look, so we took down the Mutun decorations. But we haven't settled on the roof ornament design yet.
我们想让侠士帮忙牵个线。: We would appreciate it if you help us make this connection.
我们所中之毒需要三味毒药来解。: There are three ingredients we need to counteract the poison.
我们所有的成功，都来自于后天的努力。: Everything we have achieved, we earned through our own sweat and toil.
我们拜拜，你就出现了，还帮我们找到了糖饼的消息，大家现在都安心了。: We prayed, and you appeared, and helped us get clues about our sweet pastries. We're reassured.
我们掌柜的说啦，游春时节，是否饮茶不重要，让您记住了才更重要啊。您现在有没有兴趣: Like our shopkeeper always says, what matters is not whether you drink tea during a spring outing, but whether the moment sticks with you. So, how about stopping by Wu's for a cup of tea?
我们掌柜的说大丈夫就该洗清水浴，谁劝都不听，愣是不赚这个钱。: Our innkeeper says a real man should bathe in clear water. He won't listen to anyone's advice and refuses to profit from it.
我们掘开了枯井，连通了水路，令胡杨长出了叶子，使黄金乡重现于世。: We cleared out the dried-up well, reopened the water channels, and the poplars started leafing out again—bringing the Land of Gold back to life.
我们搭起葡萄架，又把它埋在土里啦。乌云把星星吃掉了，最冷的风灌成月光酒呀。 月光: We raised a trellis for the grapes, then buried it deep in the ground. The stars faded behind the clouds, the wind turned cold as Moonlight Wine. Is fate truly so kind? A tearful figure waves goodbye, eyes glowing like rubies.

We raised a trellis for the grapes, then buried it deep in the ground. The stars vanished behind the clouds as the wind turned chillingly cold, like moonlight wine. Is fate truly so kind? A weeping figure waves goodbye as their eyes light up like rubies.
我们方才做的，不正是天下最无用但天下最有趣之事么？在我看来，当然是朋友！: What we just did back there... Wasn't that useless but fun? To me, that definitely makes us friends!
我们方才摔倒了，$T(2001)，你那边有开门的办法吗？: We slipped and fell. Think you can open the door from your side?
我们明明是救驴——救驴，懂不懂？！！: We're saving the donkeys! Saving them! Got it?!
我们是不同一般的狗。我是老大，听我的！: We're different from your average mutts. I'm the boss—listen to me!
我们是从北面来的，以前家里生意做的可大了，可惜后来到处战乱，铺子都关了。爹爹只好: We came from the north. We had a huge family business, but had to close down because of the war. My dad became an Itinerant Merchant and took us with him.
我们是吴国人，方才说的是家乡话。: We're from the Wu region, and we were speaking in our own dialect!
我们是太平书院毕业的学生，刚参加完太医署的考试。: We're actually graduates from Taiping Academy ourselves. We just finished our Imperial Medical Academy exams.
我们是小孩，你是可疑的大人，不能告诉你。: We're kids. You're an adult. That makes you suspicious.
我们是朋友吧，你愿意帮我——: Come on. We're friends, right? Won't you help me...
我们是求也无法闹也无法啊……唉……: We can't beg or protest... what can we do?
我们是要做一件大事！一件天大的事情！: We're doing something big! Something huge!
我们是运气好的，能在聆杏村讨到一份生活，可不得好好珍惜。: Lucky that we've got work in Apricot Village. So we'd better hold on to it.
我们曾因共同的愿望建造了这座城，又因不同的立场各散四方。: We once built this city for a shared dream. Now we scatter for different causes.
我们有……天子正臣……张将军、河西的节度使……会来救我们……: We have someone the court recognized... Governor Zhang of Hexi... he'll save us...
我们本在幽州……如今在这儿给晋军供上好的战马，只是……: We used to be in Youzhou. Now we're here, raising the finest warhorses for the Jin Army. It's just…
我们村武功最高的是大鹅，我若比它还会捉鱼，怎么不算夺下第一？: Goose is the most accomplished fighter we have. If I can catch more fish than Goose, why can't I be first?
我们村长可是个了不得的人。: Our village chief is quite remarkable.
我们来时，桥已损毁，只能勉力护住桥基。你们快看看，怎么修？: The bridge was already gone when we arrived. We barely secured the foundation. Can you fix it?
我们每日这么辛苦做工，还不是想让他们将来过上好日子！: We work hard every day so that they may have better lives than we did!
我们江湖有个规矩，主人请的宴，客人可不能起身。: There's a rule in the jianghu: in a feast, the guest stays seated, no getting up.
我们没抓住那小耗子……呸，小福。她，她跑那里面儿了！大侠你往那里头走，准能找见！: We couldn't catch that rat—I mean, Little Fu. She ran off deep inside! Keep going forward and you'll find her!
我们没用这些上过菜，这头我们磕不了。: We never served those dishes, so we're not kneeling for this.
我们河东八俊的功夫也曾名震江湖，如今却难寻踪迹……: The Eight Talents of Hedong once made quite a name for ourselves in the jianghu. And now, all but vanished...
我们波陈男儿都是马背上来去，哪像你们这群软脚虾。你一个外姓女人，管不到我和阿父头: Our Bodchen men ride from childhood. Unlike you people, weak as a reed. You're just an outsider. Stay out of our business.
我们游学准备回去了，但该跟着我的小师弟忽然不见了……我点了三次名，他都……: We were preparing to leave. I called roll three times, and he was just... gone...
我们溜进去，就偷……不是，就借一点点嘛。有借有还……等大伙过好这个年了，慢慢还给: We sneak in, just borrow a little, and pay it all back once everyone's fed. Borrow, not steal!
我们焱生真的长大了，看来再过几年，这“老大”的头衔，就要交给你了。: You're really growing up! Maybe you'll be the leader in just a few years.
我们爷爷辈就是老相识了！呜，老任当年可不是这样的，不然我家那妹子也不会对他心心念: Our grandpas were old friends! And back in the day, my little sister... she always had her heart set on him.
我们玩个游戏。看看谁先醉，醉到……把最重要的秘密说给朋友听。: Let's play a game. Let's see who gets drunk first...and spills their deepest secrets to a friend.
我们现在大木作最缺人，喊你来就是去帮忙做这个。: Major timberwork is desperately short-handed right now. That's why we called you to help with this.
我们现在就走，马上就走，红线最喜欢老大了！: Let's go now! Right away! You're the best!
我们现在日子好多了，别说我们，街坊邻里都有活路了。: Things are looking up these days. Not just us—the neighbors too.
我们现在这儿候着，一会儿将这几盆好的，都给蔷姐姐搬上去！: We’ll wait here for now, and later we’ll move these good pots up for Sister Qiang!
我们现在，好像真正的一家三口呀！: Look at us. We look like a real family now. The three of us!
我们生意人讲究的是和气生财: We merchants know well that fortune comes with peace.
我们的人比那老秀才的多，柴火拾的快，够给你的！: There are more of us than them, and we cut wood faster, too. Plenty to spare for you.
我们的人流血，只会叫虏人欢笑。我们的人死去，只会成为虏狗腰上的功勋。: Every drop of our blood is a joke to the enemy. Every one of our dead is just another notch on their belt.
我们的人跟到了铁匠铺那就跟丢了，只听见一声奇怪的声音，“哧”一声，像是火盆里泼了: Our people followed him to the blacksmith shop and lost track. They only heard this weird sound, like "hiss." Like water hitting a fire?
我们的同行之约已中止，流云聚散，后会有期。: Our Companion Pact has ended. We may meet again.
我们的同行之约已解散，流云聚散，后会有期。: Our Travel-Along Promise has disbanded. Clouds come and go. We shall meet again.
我们的呢？不是说有个什么，长精神的、年轻十岁的东西，嗯？: What about us? Wasn't there something that makes you ten years younger?
我们的大张将军英勇神武，为我们带来了好日子！现在大张将军要归唐了，我们要为他再唱: Our valiant Old General Zhang has brought us good days! Now that he is returning to the Tang court, let us sing it once more for him!
我们的小张将军，张淮深的名字。: Our Young General's name, Zhang Huaishen.
我们的巴掌功，是为了强身健体，为了更高效地办差，积极向上。: This palm art is for staying healthy, so we can handle our duties better and keep our spirits up.
我们的木鸢图样还没看完呢。: We haven't finished going through the wooden eagle blueprints yet.
我们的百业创建成功啦！: Our guild has been successfully established!
我们的试验记录！里面记录了山猪要烤多久才最香！: Our trial records! They've got the exact timing for the perfect roast boar in them!
我们的飞天木鸢……全完了！: Our wooden eagles are all destroyed!
我们看少东家您这些天如此忙碌，于心不忍，才决心助你一臂之力，为重建不羡仙贡献绵薄: We've seen how busy you've been, so we figured we'd step in and help rebuild Blissful Retreat.
我们看着她……和她背后受伤的灾民和将士，才醒过来。: Seeing her and the injured soldiers and commoners behind her, we finally understood.
我们看见了，“嗖”的一下！你就拿钥匙了！“哗啦”一下，你就上楼了！: We saw you! Whoosh, and you grabbed the key! Crash, and you went upstairs!
我们真正的大侠，才不屑于这些世俗的争斗呢！: A true hero wouldn't waste time on petty squabbles like this!
我们瞒着泉儿，这些没和他说呢。: We didn't tell Liquan any of it.
我们瞧着一个样: It looks just like the original.
我们神仙渡独步天下的离人泪，您看如何？: It's called "Parting Tears," the pride of Heaven's Pier. Want to give it a try?
我们种许许多多的佛花，佛花开了，真佛就会赐福给镇子。: We plant many, many buddha flowers. When they bloom, Buddha will bless our town.
我们等晴天再带大黄试试吧……: Let's wait for clear skies and try again with Da Huang.
我们约好了，等他回来，他要送我根漂亮的红缨！: He promised to bring me a beautiful red tassel when he comes back.
我们老寨主死了，该轮到他这个当儿子的挑大梁了。: Our old chief died—time for his son to take charge.
我们老板楚晖你也见着了，他比较随性，不大靠谱。楚皓大概是放心不下，所以总是三天两: You've met our boss, Chu Hui, a laid-back guy, but not exactly dependable. I guess Chu Hao worries about him, so he's always sending stuff over.
我们老板这次让我送的不是“草料”，是“豆料”呢！: Our boss didn’t send me to deliver "fodder" this time, but "bean feed"!
我们聆杏村特有的金玉羹，刚熬好不久，少侠要来一碗吗？: Our Apricot Village’s specialty, Golden Jade Soup, freshly brewed. Would you like a bowl, young hero?
Our special Golden Jade Soup from Apricot Village, freshly made. Would you like a bowl, young wanderer?
我们能一起坐飞鸡去给兔子们唱歌吗？: Can we all ride the wooden chicken and sing to the rabbits?
我们若多言半句，倒显得醉花阴气量狭小，容不下人了。: If we make a fuss, we'll only look petty. As though the Velvet Shade can't tolerate a little rivalry.
我们虽然不能真切地触碰它们，但它们的存在，依旧能指引世上的人们。: We cannot truly touch them, but their existence still guides people in this world.
我们虽然离开很久了，可他临终前还念叨着家门口的泉水声咧——: We've been away for a long time, but even on his deathbed, he kept thinking about the sound of the spring right outside the door.
我们要不想尽办法多弄些银子，怎么过日子？: If we don't figure out a way to bring in more silver, how are we supposed to survive?
我们要不，直接给官家在每个殿里都备上一套寝具，如何？: What if we just kept a set of bedding for His Majesty in every hall?
我们要把吃的攒下来，然后就不怕挨饿。: That's why we're saving food... so no one gets thrown away.
我们要盯着村口那个大坏蛋！让他再也不能做坏事！: We're gonna watch that bad guy at the village gate! We'll never let him do bad things again!
我们讨论店铺粮价，你凑上来做什么？滚一边去！: We're talking about the shop's grain prices here—why are you even sticking your nose in? Go away!
我们走到这儿看见河面上有雾，一进去，啥都看不见，拿的火把，油灯也说熄就熄，只能灰: When we got to the river, the fog was so thick we couldn't see anything. The torches and oil lamps all went out, so we had to turn back.
我们走吧，免得惹祸上身。: Let's go before we get dragged into this.
我们身上的干粮很快吃完了，其他弟弟妹妹们又还小……: Our rations ran out so fast, and the little ones are still so young...
我们过不了河，可渡河之人，何必是我们呢？我们只管带足照明之物再试一次。: We can't cross, but we don't have to be the ones who make it. Bring enough material for making light and we'll try again.
我们近日发现山门弟子为撰写论文，整日在宿舍和实验室埋头苦学，长此以往，可不利于身: We've noticed a troubling trend. Disciples hunched over desks from dawn to dusk, scribbling away. That's no way to keep body and soul together.
我们还得谢谢这张文表，送来一阵东风！: And we have Zhang Wenbiao to thank for handing us the perfect excuse.
我们还没入林呢，这就撞见了无心谷的人？: We haven't even made it into the woods yet and we're already running into Hollow Vale folks?
我们还没来得及道谢呢！: We didn't even get the chance to thank him!
我们还需要从长计议: We must plan our next move carefully.
We need to handle this carefully and think it through.
我们这些人，过去不过是蛮族的玩物，被逼着吞火玩刀子……: We were nothing more than playthings of barbarians in the past, forced to swallow fire and wield knives...
我们这些跑商的，就是要占人先机，去看看才知道有没有嘛。: We merchants need to be the first to act, to see for ourselves if we can find something.
我们这儿不比城北边儿，难得见到这么精致的东西。多少钱？我买下来，搁我们坊前面照着: We don't see craft like this on our side of town. How much? I'll take it and hang it in front of the workshop so everyone can enjoy a bit of cheer.

我壮起胆子，在这找了好久，都没找到我的剑。你呢，你看见它了吗？: I've searched everywhere but couldn't find my sword. Did you see it?
我备了些喂鸟的零嘴……偶尔喂鸟，有些鸟儿因此便常夜中来。: I keep some snacks to feed them, so a few come back night after night.
我外头有事，往后偶尔还会回来……先说正事，你为什么要修这船？破成这样……不如重新: I've got things to do out there. I'll come back now and then. But tell me, why bother fixing this? It's falling apart. Just build a new one.
我大人有大量，她今日帮了我，我就得还了这份恩再走！: I'm generous by nature. She helped me today, so I have to repay that kindness before I go!
我大半辈子了，才想明白……这年头，种地没活路！天！官！人！都要杀你！: It took me most of my life to figure it out... You can't make a living off farming these days. Seems like everyone and everything out there is going to crush you!
我大受震撼！震撼于这居然也好意思提交。: I'm shocked! Shocked that you actually dared to submit this.
我大哥就把我送来官府，说我犯了【诬陷罪】，非要官老爷还他一个清白……: My own brother hauled me off to the magistrate for [defamation], insisting the judge clear his name.
我大哥枪法绝世，却太过重情重义，这污糟军营……到底委屈了他。: My brother's unmatched with his spear, but he's weighed down by his loyalty. This miserable camp was never worthy of him.
我大哥让我在这守着，原地待命，真不该听他的！细想想，他定是怕主公将来怪罪，牵连了: He told me to wait here. I shouldn't have listened! Now I see, he was afraid the lord would punish me too.
我大哥说了，这玉石，能给人带来好运的……: My brother said it brings good luck...
我大哥身子不好，听说这池子灵得很，我来讨个吉利。: My brother's sick. People say this pond works miracles. Thought I'd try.
我大哥！你见过没？他可是天下第一枪，江湖人送绰号白马银枪，高——思——继！: Have you seen my brother? They call him the Silver Spear on Horseback, Gao Siji!
我大宋年轻一辈都能如此血勇，中原武林倒也中兴在望。: The future of Central Plains martial arts looks bright if all the young folks in Song are this brave.
我大概知道了……我们别再折腾阿黄了……: I think I understand now... let's leave Butter alone...
我大聪明这么聪明的一颗脑袋，怎能白白饿死在这儿！救命，救命啊！: I, Big Smart with my clever mind, can't just starve to death here! Help! Someone, please help!
我天……饶、饶命！: Oh heavens... please don't kill me!
我天涯之人，作天涯之游。百草野邂逅，得游侠美玉相赠，结下善缘，我心甚为感佩。天底:
As a wanderer under Heaven, I roam the ends of the earth. In the Verdant Wilds, I encountered the Youxia-er who gifted me a fine jade pendant, forging a bond of goodwill. My heart swells with gratitude. Where else under Heaven can one find such a kind soul as the Youxia-er—benevolent in heart, gentle in demeanor, and ever generous in action!

I compiled the Youxia-er's deeds into a book, which became a bestseller among merchants, spreading his virtuous name far and wide. A Swordsman from Well of Heaven, skeptical of such tales, questioned how someone neither affiliated with the Heaven's Gate nor a wealthy merchant could be so magnanimous. I answered truthfully: because he is virtuous.

Enclosed with this letter is the Youxia-er's charitable donation. When we meet again, let us dispense with formalities. The Wayfarer bows once more to the honorable Youxia-er.

我天生反骨不受教，从小就被爷娘夫子管束，没少挨骂。现在入了江湖，我可要好好痛快痛: I was born rebellious. Since childhood, my parents and teachers kept me under tight control—I've had enough scoldings from them. Now that I've entered the jianghu, I'm going to enjoy myself properly!
我太感动了，谢谢$T(3110)，谢谢药药……我一定回家把它供起来……: I'm so touched. Thank you $T(3110), thank you, Yaoyao... I'm going to take them home and enshrine them properly...
我太爷爷是羽林军队正，我爷爷是雁子都都头，我爹……我爹乃衙前讨击使，率军镇守阳城: My great-grandfather served in the Feathered Guards. My grandfather led the Wild Goose Division. My father held Yangcheng and killed over a thousand of your kind. The Luo family has fought for three generations. We do not kneel!
我头一回来驻地……没想到这就是我们九流门的地盘，还挺气派的嘛。: It's my first time here... didn't know this was our headquarters. Impressive!
我头一回走商，你们去哪儿我就去哪儿。最后回哪儿，我也都成。: This is my first time on a caravan… I'll go wherever you go. I'm fine with wherever we return.
我夸你你应着便是，这么不爽利，还怎么自称大侠？: Just say thank you when I praise you! How can you be a Great Hero if you don't accept people's admirations?
我女儿德行有亏，竟与一个连饭都吃不起的江湖人夜中相会，私定终身！: My daughter has disgraced herself, sneaking out at night to meet some penniless swordsman and making secret promises!
我好不容易抢到了今年这最后一对，你瞧——: I fought so hard to grab the last pair this year, look!
我好不容易放下的刀，你别再拿起来了。就当是，为天下人。: Putting down the sword wasn't easy. Don't you pick it up again. For the good of the world.
我好像……梦到了一种能吞食所有痛苦的虫子。: I dreamed of a worm... A worm that eats sorrow.
我好像忘记了一件事……<指着心口>这里……就是这里，: I think I forgot something... <pointing to heart> Here... right here...
我好像还是没弄懂，我们的家乡在哪里，回家的路在哪里呢？: I don't know where home is yet. Don't know how to find the way back.
我好像闻到了一种奇怪的味道，好复杂，似乎是很多种香料，还有大火爆炒的油烟气。这是: I think I smell something odd. It's... complicated. Spices, maybe, and the kind of smoke you get from a hot wok. What is that?
我好像，已经学会了。: I think... I've already got it.
我好几次差点儿逮住他，偏生他滑不溜手，一眨眼就不见了！: I've nearly caught him several times, but he's slippery as an eel—gone in a flash!
我好容易遇着一个，可不得从娃娃抓起。: I finally found someone like that, so I have to hold on while we're still young!
我好心好意救你们，你们居然恩将仇报，手段还如此恶毒！: I saved all of you, and this is how you repay me? With such cruelty!
我好心学做汤，她怎么还骂我傻子，你说她到底啥意思啊。: I was being nice learning to make soup, and she called me a fool. What did she really mean?
我好心帮你，你居然……: I tried to help you, and you...
我好心给他们治病……怎么一个一个病没好就想着回家？: I tried to cure them, but they all just want to go home before they're healed.
我好想她……她这一辈子吃了太多苦，最后却没吃到几口甜。: I miss her so much... She suffered so much in her life and never got a taste of sweetness in the end.
我好着呢！小粟，不怪你，是这个人——: I'm fine. Totally fine. Su, it's not your fault. It was that person...
我好饿啊……我已经把剩余的兽肉和野菜都给你了，不要再等待了，快开始吧！: I'm so hungry... I've already given you the remaining meat and vegetables. Let's start now!
我如今已经不懂什么叫悲伤，心不再会痛。: With all that suffering, I'm already too miserable to feel any pain.
我如今易容的这人可还是你的徒弟？: Is this guy your disciple too? The guy I'm disguised as?
我如今连三娘那寻死觅活的相思病都治得，怎么不算法力精深？: I just cured Sanniang's lovesickness. That takes real skill.
我如青山如盗: I am like the green mountains, like a thief
我妹妹她才那么小，饿得嘴唇发白也记得把饼子留给我，烧得浑身滚烫，还记得伸手替妈擦: My sister is so little... Even when she was starving, she saved her bread for me. Even burning up with a fever, she still tried to wipe my mom's tears...
我妻子托人送了信来，她想好了要做一番事业，我须得陪着她。茶摊，自然也不能开了。: My wife sent a letter through someone. She's decided to start a business, and she needs me with her. Naturally, the tea stall will have to close.
我姊妹二人供灯的诚心，便换来了这样的果？: I and my sister lit lamps with sincerity... yet the result? Karma is strange.
我姓霍，当然是我当将军。: My surname is Huo, so of course I'll be the general.
我姥爷挖了一辈子，自己没吃上过一口。我爹娘也没吃过。: My grandpa dug his whole life… never tasted a single drop. My parents neither.
我娘也这么说……那稻穗低头，关我啥事啊！我又不姓稻。: My mother said that too. But what's that got to do with me? I ain't no crop!
我娘交给我一个秘密任务……为了百姓的安危，我要不着痕迹地潜伏在人群中……: My mother gave me a secret mission. For the safety of everyone, I must blend into the crowd.
我娘亲答应我，让徐叔教我本事。: Mother promised that Uncle Xu would pass on his skills to me.
我娘啊，成日爱说人就一个家，人呐，活着在家，死了也得在家。: She used to say we have only one home, and we should stay here, whether in life or in death.
我娘在这儿活了大半辈子了……: My mother spent most of her life here.
我娘当年就在不死树那儿采叶子，之后挎着篮子，风风火火地四处寻我。: Back then, my mom was picking leaves at the immortal tree. Carried that basket and went all over looking for me.
我娘成日要把隔壁家王小美带到家里来，相中了就知道撮合我俩。: My mother keeps talking about bringing Wang Xiaomei from next door over, maybe setting us up.
我娘病了好些日子，求求贵人，赏些药钱。: My mom's been sick for days... Please, kind person, can you spare a coin for some medicine.
我娘的难道就不是我的？猪蹄送到她面前，我要吃，难道我娘还会不给我？: Isn't my mother's food mine too? Sure, you bring them for her, but if I wanted some, would my own mother refuse me?
我娘织布的时候它陪着，我爹钓鱼的时候它陪着，现在他们两个都被那只坏猫迷得神魂颠倒: She's with my mom when she's weaving, and with my dad when he's fishing. Now they're both completely smitten with that awful cat!
我娘给我吃的面，不是这个味。: The noodles my mom made never tasted like this.
我娘被我问住了。她想了想，指着这栋楼说，这首歌和这栋楼一样。: My mother didn't know what to say. She thought for a while, then pointed at that tower. She said the song's like the tower.
我娘让我干的，嘿嘿。我爹老偷偷藏酒，我把它们都倒了，我娘可高兴了！: My mother told me to do it, haha. My father always keeps a secret stash of wine. Pouring it out makes my mother very happy.
我娘说了，你根本没有金叶子，不死树也没叶子。: My mom says you don't have any gold leaves, and the immortal tree doesn't have leaves either.
我娘说了，光靠飞鼠可不行，还得自己努力。: My mama says the squirrel can only do so much. You've still got to put in the work yourself.
我娘说啦，是不羡仙好心收留她，要不然她这样貌在外面还不知道会受什么欺负呢。我们这: My mom said it was nice of the Blissful Retreat to take her in. With a face like that, who knows what would've happened to her out there.
我娘说啦，这叫丑人多作怪！: As my mom says, "Homely folks tend to create drama!"
我娘说过，做菜这事，这食材差上一分一毫，都不一样。: My mom always said, even the smallest change in ingredients makes all the difference.
我娘说，不可以和陌生人打架。: My mom says I shouldn't fight strangers.
我娘说，不问自取就是偷。: My mom says taking things without asking is stealing.
我娘说，官家年轻那会儿也四处闯荡，还在我家赊过账嘞。: My mother says the Emperor used to wander the roads himself, back in the day. Even ran up a tab at our place.
我娘说，爹爹从前帮她助威的时候最心动，{0}的心动瞬间呢？: Mom says dad helping her in fights was the most romantic. When did {0}'s heart skip?
我娘说，越饱满的稻穗垂得越低，可我再弯下去，头都要磕地上了……: My mother always said, "The fuller the grain, the lower it bends." But if I bend any more, my head'll be in the dirt.
我娘说，这个鱼叫黄河大鲤鱼。探花使吃了，会不会变成黄河大猫咪？: My mom says this kind of fish is called the Yellow River Carp. If Scout eats it, will it turn into a Yellow River Catfish?
我娘说，随便拿别人东西的是小贼。: My mom says people who take what isn't theirs are thieves.
我娘走前……划了几道字画似的……: Before my mother passed, she left behind a mark that resembled a written character...
我娘跟我说过，凡是比生母年轻的，一律称姐姐，凡是比外祖母年轻的，一律称嫂子！: My mother taught me: if a woman's younger than your mother, call her sister; if she's younger than your grandmother, call her Madam!
我婆娘在田里呢，我打完这局就去做活。: My wife's working the fields. I'll head out after this hand.
我婆娘在田里呢，我打完这局就去做活，你要不也来一局！: My wife's working the fields. I'll head out after this hand. Want to join in?
我媳妇不一直在我身旁待着吗？: Isn't my wife always by my side?
我媳妇就这性子，爱乱丢东西，还从不告诉我。: She always leaves things lying around and never tells me where.
我媳妇走的时候……才二十出头……我都没让她过上好日子……: My wife was only in her early twenties when she died... I never gave her a good life...
我媳妇，这娘们整日想东想西，把自己身子想坏了咋整，老子还得伺候她一辈子。: That's my wife... always fretting. If she breaks down, I'll be stuck caring for her.
我嫌你们聒噪，特意踢了踢马肚子，想着赶紧走快点……: I grew impatient with your worries and spurred my horse forward…
我孤云一派专研天文历法之学，能为《应天历》之编撰尽力，亦是荣幸。: Our order has devoted itself to astronomy and calendar science for generations. It is an honor to contribute to this work.
我学不来那些，好了，师兄别说我了，你呢？你的天下均水，是不是可以开始了？: That's beyond me. Enough about my shortcomings. What about you? Is the time right for your Waters of the World?
我学这东西做什么？: Why would I want to learn this?
我守时嘛……当初说好这个时辰收工的，多一分一秒都不是这个时辰。: I'm only keeping to the agreed time. We said we would wrap up at this hour. Once even a second passes, it's no longer the same time.
我完成了陛下的旨意。: I carried out His Majesty's will.
我定然前往拜访，多谢游侠！: I'll visit them right away. Thank you for telling me!
我定要查出是谁浇的，让他好好舔上一日冰柱的甜味！: I will find out who did it and make them lick that post for a whole day!
我定要给狗崽子们，都找个好归宿。: I'll find a good home for every last pup.
我实在……实在是走投无路，怕耽搁了声声治病，才斗胆相求。: I truly had nowhere else to turn. I only dared to make this bold request of you because I was afraid of delaying Shengsheng's treatment.
我实在……放不下……: I really can't let it go...
我实在舍不得，给她买胭脂，帮她画眉，好让旁人瞧不出来……: I couldn't stand it. So I bought her rouge and helped her draw her eyebrows, just so others wouldn't see how sick she really was.
我宣布，剩下的人，你们可以进入谢某第二轮考验！: The rest of you are moving on to the second test!
我宣布，获胜的是……: I hereby announce the winner is—
我宣布，运输任务暂停。: I hereby declare the transport mission... suspended.
我害了他们……就像当年……我亲手……亲手解决了自己疯狂的儿子……: I brought this on them... Just like back then, when I... when I had to put an end to my son's madness...
我家中有个小弟，幼日素爱与我玩闹……那时候，我们也配合得极好。: I have a little brother at home who loved playing with me when he was small... Back then, we worked together perfectly.
我家乖女真是长大了不少啊，祖母心里欢喜得很……: My granddaughter has grown so much. I am so happy for you…
我家人在那里，我要去找她。还请冯大哥帮我一帮。: I have family there. I need to find her. Please help me.
我家公子是那城东的郑公子，他和这青蛟堂堂主交好，差我来看看有什么能帮得上的。: He is Master Zheng from the east side of town. He's close with the master of the Jade Serpent Hall and sent me to see if I could lend a hand.
我家公子的戏，你不配听！: You don't deserve to watch our master's perform!
我家囡囡在席上……席上……不好……我去救囡囡。: My little girl was at the banquet... the banquet... No... I need to save her.
我家囡囡快回来了吗？: Is my little girl coming home soon?
我家囡囡怎么还没有回家哟 你见着我家囡囡了吗: Why isn't my daughter home yet? Have you seen her anywhere?
我家在开封城郊置办了套宅子，能望见平野原上连绵金穗，好看得很呢！: We have a place just outside Kaifeng. From there, you can look out over the fields, all golden with wheat stretching as far as you can see. Truly a beautiful sight!
我家在遥远的北方，那里原来水草丰美，牛羊成群，可后来一场大灾，我们的牛羊都死了…: My home is way up north. It used to be fertile, with abundant water and grass, full of cattle and sheep. But then a terrible disaster struck, and we lost all our livestock...
我家地共五十三亩，我数三十个数，你要是报不出我家下回该纳多少柴草布粮，我便跟乡里: My family's got fifty-three mu of land. I'll count to thirty, if you can't tell me exactly what I owe in firewood, cloth and grain, I'll tell the whole village you're a fraud!
我家境贫寒，却一心向学，常常饿着肚子， 拿省下的钱去换书。: My family's always been poor, but I've stayed focused on my studies. I'd often go hungry to save up for more books.
我家大业大，打听一个人的生死，又有何难？: With all my money and connections, finding out if someone's dead or alive is easy.
我家大人很忙，没空管我，你不用担心，我堂兄会来接我的！他叫祁秋亦！: My adults are busy and don't watch me. Don't worry though, my cousin will come get me! His name is Qi Qiuyi!
我家大人请青溪圣手出马，有你什么事！还不快滚！: My master has summoned the Divine Healer of Silver Needle—What business is it of yours?! Scram, now!
我家娃不是从小爱起夜吗，胆又小，总要我陪他去。我就好几次瞧见，半夜有人偷偷摸黑来: My kid is always scared at night and needs me to go with him to the bathroom. A few times, I caught sight of someone sneaking over to the chief's place late at night.
我家娘子……那是出了名儿的剽悍……少侠你看，是不是……: My wife... she's famously fierce... so, could you maybe...
我家娘子今儿不在，我做主，定给客官一个最低价！: My wife is not around today, so I'm calling the shots. I promise you won't find a better price anywhere!
我家婆娘还在等我，不跟你耗！: My wife's waiting for me, I don't have time for this!
我家媳妇吧，嗜鱼如命，平日里除了鱼，什么都不吃。: My wife is crazy about fish. She hardly eats anything else.
我家孙子病了，我去善妙洲采药，结果遭遇了一伙契丹人。我藏在草丛里，可还是被他们发: My grandson was sick, so I went to Sundara Land to gather herbs. I saw a group of Khitan there, and I hid in the grass... but they still found me. I was too afraid to watch, so I shut my eyes.
我家小姐已将白家那秃驴送进官府了！那白秃驴，果真不怀好意！他暗中设局，原是想要害: My young lady handed that scoundrel over to the authorities! Turns out he really was scheming! He tried to frame our lord for death!
我家小姐正是二八年华，如花美眷！莫说男子，便是女子也有上门提亲的。: Our young lady is in the prime of her youth, a true beauty! Not just men, even women come to propose.
我家小娘子哪哪儿都好，可偏偏是个说风就是雨的性子。前儿个听了一出女侠聂隐娘的书，: Our young lady is perfect in every way, except for her rashness. Just recently, she heard the story of the warrior Nie Yinniang and all she could talk about was setting off into the jianghu...
我家小虎，自两岁开蒙，每日读书要戌时，如今已经会读四书啦……: My little Tiger started his schooling when he was just two, and now he studies every day until evening. He can already read the Four Books!

Patar taught me this was a fool's bargain, a trade destined for loss.

In the desert, a merchant follows water. Water draws people, and people are the source of all wealth.
Their wells became my trade routes. Their sacrifice gave me Poplar Bazaar.
It is time to settle my account.

This departure will be long. I wonder, will I see the poplars green again?
I must believe so. I believe in my own strength, and I believe in his vow.
"Sentiment is a weakness in our trade," my Patar used to say. But look how far it has brought me.
From Hexi to Chang'an, to Jingchu and beyond. My road is long yet.

I'm just a waiter. Working here, you see all kinds of things. This is a place where anything can be bought—a dog, a person, or, for the right price, a person turned into a dog.
But the strangest deal I ever saw began the day a body lay at our doorstep. It looked more beast than human, torn and bleeding. Around here, that's nothing new—just our turn to clean up the mess. 
The boss went to kick it aside, but it bared its teeth, and a silver ingot rolled to his feet. Miss Chun bought that body with that piece of silver. She carried the girl herself, blood soaking her clothes and coins. 
A poor bargain, but Miss Chun didn't care. She taught the girl to walk, to read, to live. When the girl vanished, Miss Chun went door to door, banging on gates, scaring half-dressed men out of their wits. The girl always returned after dark with a bunch of cheap white flowers in hand.
She stayed one long spring—long enough for forsythia to bloom and wither, long enough for the girl to speak. They say her first word was "Chun (spring)." But to me, it was "money." 
"How much," she asked, "to buy spring?"

我等时间，等了一辈子。 \n等到手中的唐旗已暌违这片土地，近一个甲子。 \n人言:
I have waited a lifetime—  
waiting until the Tang banner I once held has long since vanished from this land, almost sixty years gone.  
They say a man knows his destiny by fifty. But what I waited for was no simple fate ordained by heaven.  
So I wrestled with time itself—even if it meant forsaking my compassion, wielding power ruthlessly, sacrificing... my eldest brother.  
No, even if it meant sacrificing myself. Liangzhou could do without me. The Guiyi Army could do without me.  
But the sacred oath to reclaim our homeland still demands a torchbearer.  
And today, I wait for that successor to appear.  
Yet the one I await still carries the fire of innocence—and a deep respect for me.  
The hostage in Chang'an must never become a weakness for our cause.  
So I laid bare the truth before him—the noble and the sordid alike.  
I want him to abandon me, just as I abandoned my brother.  
  
If every passing of the torch must be bathed in blood, then let mine stain the path ahead—  
until he rises above my old allies, eclipsing even my own renown.  
I watch his loyal guards standing sentry outside, watch him silence the voices opposed to my return to Tang.  
He is proving himself worthy indeed.  
I once thought his arrival would come with a blade at my throat—  
but instead, he handed the blade into my hands.  
I know this blade too well. At our first farewell, it was my brother who gave it to me.  
Later, I passed it on to my brother's son.  
And now, it has come full circle—back into my grasp.  
He vows to lead the Guiyi Army, waiting for the day I come home.  
In that moment, we understood one another completely.  
From now on, through all the miles that lie ahead, no matter the distance, we will stand side by side.

我虽未直接杀他，他却因我而死……满身罪孽抵赖不得。如今守着这骸骨，也是为了赎罪…: I did not kill him… yet he died because of me. I could never cast off that sin. For all these years, I have kept his remains with me, only to repent.
我虽然不懂写话本，但小时候我练武遇到瓶颈的时候，就喜欢跑到林子里，追追小鸟，找找: I don't know much about writing, but when I hit a wall in training as a child, I'd run off into the woods and chase birds for a while.
我虽然很穷，但是不需要帮助，我还能过得下去！: Poor as I am, I don't need charity. I can manage on my own.
我虽然找人传了口信，但他还没来过临江驿，想来这会儿应在路上了。: I sent word, but he's never been to Riverside Station before, so he's probably on his way here now.
我虽眼花了，但记性不差！不对，你是谁？你不是天裁？: My eyesight might not be great, but my memory's just fine! Wait. Who are you, really? You're not Tiancai, are you?
我行我令，天下非攻。: I issue my own decree: let all offensive wars cease and peace prevail beneath the heavens.
我行我素啊……那便是从“我”，合一个“鹅”字（轻笑）。: Does as it pleases... Well, there's only one creature with that kind of pride. A goose. (soft laugh)
我行走江湖的时候，你可还没出生呢，想抢我？再去练个二十年吧！: I was out adventuring before you were even born. You want to rob me? Come back after you've trained for another twenty years!
我表哥他……他和一般人不一样，他脑子不太好，有点儿傻……: My cousin... he's a little different. His mind's a bit slow...
我袖撒点小慌: I'll tell a little white lie
我被人喂了毒药，不拿张淮深的人头去见，不久就会毒发而死。: They poisoned me. I bring them Zhang Huaishen's head, or I die.
我被母羊奶大，第一次用弯刀却是剔它的骨。: A ewe nursed me. First time I used a blade was to strip her bones.
我被混进来的贼人打晕关在了附近的箱子。是这位小兄弟救了我。: The intruder knocked me out and locked me in a crate nearby. This one here pulled me out.
我要……回……家……长安……回……: I must... get... home... Chang'an... home...
我要……把大姐姐娶回家！: I want... to marry her and bring her home with me!
我要上织网！: I need to get my paper published!
我要上集市去！娘给的钱能买十个糖画！: I'm going to the market! The money Mom gave me can buy ten sugar paintings!
我要下井……况且我走不走，与你不相干。: I'm going down. What I do is my business.
我要代表妙妙喵惩罚你！: In the name of Meow Meow, I'll punish you!
我要你为我做一件事，我算你做到了。: I asked you for a favor, and you delivered.
我要你分十支队伍，越过沦陷之地，甚至假道回鹘。此行危险，无异于苏武出使——: I need you to divide your forces into ten teams, crossing the occupied territories and even seeking passage through the Oghuz lands. This mission is perilous, no less than Su Wu's.
我要你画完这幅画……它是我要的答案，也是你要的答案。: I need you to finish this painting... It is the answer I am seeking, as well as the answer you are seeking.
我要你，画完这幅画。: I need you to finish this painting.
我要保佑我的姐妹和她的心上人长长久久、此生朝暮！: I wish for my sister and her beloved to share a long and happy life together!
我要再团大一点……: I'm going to make the next one bigger...
我要写个话本子，就写，一位少年将军的父亲为其叔父所害，但叔父对他又有养育之恩……: I should write a story: a young general whose father died because of his uncle, but the uncle raised him...
我要出人头地，给我娘过上好日子，当大官，让我娘和我、张安康、周娟一辈子都不受人欺:
I want to be successful so my mother can live a better life. If I can become an official, then my mother, Zhang Ankang, Zhou Juan, and I will never be looked down upon again. —Lu San'er 
I will never become a cook. —Zhang Ankang 
I want to live long and make the man just ahead marry me. —Zhou Juan 
I hope the trees bless Shusheng so that he will never leave me. —Liu Yueying 
Come home... Come home... —Pan Gui 
I hope my baby comes home... To see their mother... —Wu Caifeng 
Don't hit me! I'm on great terms with Liquan! —Fen 
Please don't fight, and I hope you stay in good health. —Zhang Quan

我要出去一趟，不知道什么时候回来。: I'm going away for some time. I can't say when I'll return.
我要单间（单人玩法）: I'd like a single room (Solo Mode)
我要卖些货物: I'd like to sell some goods
我要去南边了，南边暖和，用不着这个了，大侠还留在北边，给更多人报仇……嗯，给你！: I'm going south where it's warm, so I don't need this anymore. You're staying up here in the cold... here, take it!
我要去告诉我爹！: My dad's going to hear about this!
我要去告诉爹爹，你欺负我！: I'm telling Dad you were mean to me!
我要去告诉长老！: I'm going straight to the elders!
我要去找他算账！: I'm going to make them pay!
我要去找李安哥哥了，下次见呀！: I'm going to go find Brother Li An. See you next time!
我要去找母亲教训你这只坏鹅！！！: I'm going to tell my mother to teach you, you bad goose!!!
我要去找江叔！江叔从来不会这样对我！！: I'm going to Uncle Jiang! He would never treat me like this!
我要去樊楼做一件事，你知道樊楼怎么走吗？: I need to go to Revelry Hall for something. You know the way?
我要去水里，我健步如飞……: Into the water I go. In the water, I can run...
我要去看我藏起来的那些名字。: I need to check the names I've hidden.
我要去给归义军报信，我家大人被扣在甘州了。: I need to inform the Guiyi Army that my master has been detained in Ganzhou.
我要去赚钱啊！: I've got to earn a living!
我要去黑水城，我得送东西咧！: I need to go to Black Water City… gotta deliver something!
我要听小酒哥哥的新故事。: I want to hear Brother Jiu's new story.
我要告诉我爹去！: Wait till my dad hears about this!
我要告诉长老去！: The elders will hear about this!
我要和你说的是这个——喏，那天从残垣找到的匣子。: This is what I wanted to show you. See? The case I found in the ruins that day.
我要和阿泉一起去，一起回！谁也不许掉队！: Yes, I'll go with Little Quan, and we'll all come back together. No one will be left behind.
我要回家。: I just want to go home.
我要回家，我要找阿娘！: I want to go home! I want my mom!
我要在这里行一千台阶，哭一万声息，求得高僧妙善相顾，帮我解救失散的恋人。: I swore I'd climb a thousand steps and cry ten thousand tears, just to catch the eye of the monk Miaoshan, so he'd help me find my lost love.
我要外出几日，把你送去不羡仙……: I'm going away for a few days. I'll bring you to Blissful Retreat…
我要带奶奶坐云槎，上墨城去哩！: I'm taking Granny on the Sky Shuttle to visit Mohist City!
我要悄悄作工，然后惊艳所有人！: I'll sneak in and work so well it'll stun the lot of them!
我要成为晦谷最了不起的学者……等着瞧吧！！: I'll become the greatest scholar of Mirkvale. I swear!!
我要找寒娘子告状去！: I'm telling Madam Han about this!
我要把你的脸撕下来做成面具！: I'll rip your face off and make a mask out of it!
我要把它们都记牢，这样下次书院会考，才能拿第一呀！: I need to remember them all so I can get first place in the next Academy exam!
我要把这人间烟火刻进楠木，凿入顽石。: I want to etch this peaceful life into wood and stone.
我要把这染布的手艺传下去，这样才对得起师傅。: I'll pass on this dyeing craft. Only way to honor the one who taught me.
我要拯救全江湖，获得爹爹的认可，然后迎娶李安哥哥！: I want to save the entire jianghu, earn Dad's approval, And then... and make Brother Li An my husband!
我要捞那只！那只好看！: I want to catch that one! That one looks good!
我要摘一束最美的花，送给最美的寒姨，我和寒姨天下第一好！嘿嘿嘿……: I'm going to pick the most beautiful flower and give it to the most beautiful Aunt Han. Aunt Han and I are the closest! Heh heh...
我要整不薯条: I want a whole order of fries.
我要是一辈子都穿一件衣服，是不是也不用再纠结穿什么了？: If I wear the same clothes for the rest of my life, will I never have to worry about what to wear again either?
我要是不还，你自可以去卖这酒，若遇上识货的，这酒或许能保你下半辈子衣食无忧。: Then sell the wine. If you find the right buyer, it could keep you fed and clothed for the rest of your life.
我要是怀疑你，还能跟你说这么多？实在是人手紧缺，这才麻烦少侠跑这一趟，毕竟也是为: If I suspected you, would I tell you this? We're short-handed. That's why I need you to go. It's for the people in the east city!
我要是有本事探听到这些，还能留在这里？既来之，则安之吧！: If I had the connections to find that out, would I still be sitting here? We're here, so we might as well make peace with it.
我要是穷奇师，就不会只说要建防御机巧！就不会让我弟子被欺负！穷奇师哪受得了我这气: If I were them, I'd do a lot more than build walls! I wouldn't let my disciples get pushed around! The Artificers wouldn't put up with this garbage!
我要是说了，你们还能陪我唠这么久。: If I'd told you earlier, would you have spent so much time chatting with me?
我要有你这手艺，速度不知道快多少！: If I had your skill, I'd be ten times faster!
我要正式上门提亲求娶沈姑娘……: I want to officially ask for Miss Shen's hand in marriage...
我要照着你做一个射日神弩！: I'm going to build a sun-shooting crossbow in your honor!
我要用九十九只红色烟花，给蔷姑娘摆一颗巨大的爱心啊！: I'm going to use ninety-nine red fireworks to make a giant heart for her!
我要用最好的华裳给她鼓劲！: I want to gift her the finest clothes to make her shine!
我要的东西，可不好找。: What I want is not easy to find.
我要的消息呢？: What about the information I asked for?
Where’s the information I asked for?
我要的答案呢: Where's the answer I've been looking for?
我要的铜板，都拿到了吗？: Got all the coins I asked for?
我要知道，还用得着和你在这儿猜？也不知是他自己想走，还是被师傅赶的……: If I knew, why would I be guessing with you? I wonder if he wants to leave, or if Master wants him to leave…
我要第一个买到话本: I'm gonna be first in line to buy it!
我要等着哥哥们回来……或是，等着神女的启示……: I'll wait for my brothers to come back... or for the goddess to show me the way...
我要给他看看……他当时骗了我的东西，现在我不怕了，我懂了……我……不怕了……: I want to show it to him, the one who tricked me before. Now, I'm not afraid anymore. I get it... I'm not scared anymore.
我要继续研究风的力量，以致飞天。: I will continue to pursue the secrets of the wind, so that one day I might fly among the clouds.
我要跟林哥哥一起去南边了，我爹在南边等咱们呢。大侠，你也一起走吗？: I'm going south with Brother Lin. My papa is waiting for us down there. Why don't you come too?
我要这个！和比翼双飞的烟火一起放，一定好看！: I want this! Setting it off with the fireworks of flying side by side will surely look amazing!
我要这天再遮不住我眼！: You need no ring to rule them all.
我要送的，乃是从海外运来的上上品珍珠！那珠闪的哟，和天上的月亮似的。: I've brought her precious pearls from overseas! They shine like the moon in the sky!
我要通铺（三人玩法）: I'd like a shared room (3-Player Mode)
我要都买下来，送给惜春！: I plan to buy it and give it to Xichun.
我要醉花阴姐姐的红包！: I want Velvet Shade Sister's Red Packet!
我要飞得更高，更高！: Higher! I want to go higher!
我见东阙公子，也是为了她。: She's the reason I want to meet the Ember of East...
我见你也在一旁听了一会儿了，你能听明白他说什么吗？: I noticed you've been listening for a while now. Did you understand what he was saying?
我见你入谷之后久未回来，实在放心不下……但看来是我多虑了。: You were gone so long after entering the valley—I couldn't help but worry... Yet it seems my fears were unfounded.
我见你几次三番都能将我擒住，功夫一定了得。若你肯信我，明晚来伏马庄寻我，我们一齐: You've caught me several times already; you must be pretty good. If you're willing to trust me, come to Finesteed Hamlet tomorrow night. We'll head to his place together and get to the bottom of this.
我见你在梦里上天入地，乐而忘返不是么？: You were having quite the adventure in that dream, weren't you?
我见你大道理那么多，还以为螳螂捕蝉，黄雀在后之事你很熟呢。怎么，只许你当黄雀，不: You speak as if you're some master strategist. What, you think only you can win?
我见少侠射箭时身手了得，求少侠帮我寻些蹊跷，敲响那太平钟。: I saw how skilled you were with a bow, Young Hero. Would you help me find some oddities to ring the Peace Bell?
我见的阵仗，可比这大多了。: I've seen much worse than this.
我见过一模一样的人: I've met someone who looks just like that
我见过你，带着她们，从北到南，走了很远。: I've seen you. You carried those two girls a long way, from the north all the way south.
我见过的江湖情缘可多了，你和你的有缘人又是哪一种呢？: I've seen many kinds of bonds in the Jianghu. What type do you and your soulmate have?
我见过相亲要房子要马车的，倒是没见过你这样的。你真的是来相亲的？: I've seen people demanding houses and wagons at a matchmaking, but never someone like you. Are you really here to find a spouse?

Tomorrow is the sect's Day of Reckoning. Have you, too, fallen into endless suffering, unfit to bear your shame? If so, Senior Brother and I would be happy to ferry you across... with our puppet strings.
我观兄台之衣饰，可是天泉弟子？但这小剑……似是孤云之物。: Looking at your attire, brother, are you a Well of Heaven disciple? This sword...it seems like it's from Lone Cloud.
我观察了山脚的村子许久，发现有个小丫头，父母外出，没人陪，总是哭闹。: I've been watching the village at the foot of the mountain. There's a girl whose parents are away. She's always alone and always crying.
我观少侠似有佛缘，不知想请哪尊回家？: I sense you have Buddha nature. Which statue would you like to take home?
我观少侠英姿飒爽，定是不凡人物。若是怜悯小老儿，就请帮帮老儿我吧！: Young wanderer, you look heroic—You must be someone remarkable. If you pity me, an old man, please help!
我观此地距离瑶光池也不远，若是能架设悬撞，也许我们就可以飞过天险。: The Alkaid Pool isn't far from here. If we set up a zipline, we could clear the gap entirely.
我观足下，连知书的本领都没有，想掉书袋都没法啊。: From what I see, you wouldn't know a book if it hit your head, can't fake being smart!
我觉得…你不像是这样的人。但是阿爹和娘亲不会骗我，所以我要好好想一想。: I feel like...You're not that type of person. But mom and dad wouldn't lie to me. I need to think this over carefully.
我觉得你这症状，应当是——: I think your symptoms point to...
我觉得刚刚那碗饸饹面更好，又香又顶饱！: Though honestly, I think that bowl of noodles I just had was even better, so flavorful and filling!
我觉得可以用中心轴将十个货箱链接起来，由一个木螂在最开头拖动，将大大提升运货速率: I could link ten cargo crates on a central axle and let a single Wooden Mantis haul the whole chain. The hauling speed would go through the roof!
我觉得快挖到水了，你下去帮我看看呗: I think I'm close to hitting water. Would you help me take a look?
我觉得煦叔说得有道理！如果以后我真的去不了太医署，那我便帮小紫打理药房和书院。: I think he's right. So if I don't end up joining the Imperial Medical Academy... I'll help Xiaozi run the pharmacy and the school.
我觉得老爷爷很有心意。: I think old grandpa was very thoughtful.
我觉得自己太紧绷了，破天荒的想游历一番，或许……游历换个环境，会让我更加放松，更: I realized I'd been way too stressed. For the first time ever, I'm thinking about traveling. Maybe a change of scenery will help me relax and see my path more clearly.
我觉得还是做云槎划算些，木鸢我已经坠了五架了……: I'll take the Sky Shuttle any day. I've crashed five Wooden Eagles already.
我觉得还是木鸢靠谱些，虽说可能摔断腿，但是至少不会在长老课上迟到……: I still say Wooden Eagles are more reliable. You might break a leg, but at least you won't be late for the Elder's lecture.
我觉得，你以后还是少看些这类的话本，也少将这些故事说给别人听。: Honestly, I think you'd be better off reading and sharing fewer stories like these.
我觉着啊…不如把圆圆叫来…或许比父母有用的多……: I think... If Yuanyuan came, it'd help more than calling his parents over.
我觉着成！老板，我们今日就把这新营生做起来！我现在就去门口宣传宣传！: I'm in! Let's get this started today! I'll go drum up interest at the gate right now!
我觉着还是咱这儿好，最近残垣里边可不太平。: I'd rather stay put. Things have been rough over in the Ruins lately.
我言怀瑾虽称不上纵横江湖，却也算仗义执言、古道热肠。: Though not famous in the jianghu, I have always spoken justly and acted with integrity.
我警告你，过路的别多管闲事！: I'm warning you! Just keep walking and mind your own business!
我认得你，只是你不认得我。: I know you, but you don't know me.
我认得这个纸鹊，是雪儿叠的！: I know this paper crane! Xue made it!
我认得，是神猫！快追！: I know that one! That's the divine cat! Get it!
我认识崔小晋的家人，他们一直在找他。: I know Cui Xiaojin's family. They've been looking for him.
我认错了，是我认错人了！大侠，我错了，别打了！: I was wrong. I mistook you for someone else! Please, Great Hero, don't hurt me!
我让你仔细看着的……这下可好！: I told you to keep watch. What are we to do now?
我让你走了嘛: Did I say you could leave?
我让她穿上那“天蚕寒衣”，亲自跟我对剑！: I made her wear it and duel me herself!
我让我的同道帮你一起寻一寻……: I'll have my people help you look.
我记得……天火落下前一日，妙善曾在村外呼喊。有人摆脱了执迷，随妙善走了。而剩下的: I remember... The day before the fire fell, Miaoshan called out from beyond the village. Some broke free from their obsessions and followed him. Those who remained felt this wind.
我记得上次出山的是谁来着？好像是叫容鸢的弟子。听说最后也没了……哎……: Who was it that went down the mountain last time? Murong Yuan, I think. Heard that ended badly too...
我记得上次吵架的原因还是因为上次吵架: I remember the reason for the last argument was still because of the last argument.
我记得他媳妇走得早。这些年，他既当爹又当娘，一个人把小易拉扯大，不容易啊。: I remember his wife died early. He's raised Xiaoyi on his own all these years. It hasn't been easy.
我记得你，也记得这个地方。就是这附近，就是你，我莫名其妙成了一扇门的学徒工！: I remember you, and I remember this place. It was right around here that you roped me into an apprenticeship with the Order of The Gateway!
我记得冯大哥他……好像也没说他的火箭已经成功了吧？: Come to think of it, Feng never actually said the flaming arrow worked, did he?
我记得去年这时候是有寒瓜的？今年怎么没了？: I remember last year around this time you had that special watermelon. How come you don't have it now?
I remember last year around this time you had that special winter melon. How come you don’t have it now?
我记得咱们家就是这个位置啊……怎么变成议事屋了？: I'm pretty sure our home used to be right here... Why does it look so different now?

In my life, I've eaten all I wanted, played all I wanted, and seen all I wanted. But whenever I think of that distant rainy night, that strange woman who fell into the river... I feel I still haven't seen enough. 

That night, I was chiseling jade from the mountain. Suddenly, a violent storm erupted. As I was about to find a cave to take shelter, a thunderbolt crashed, my hanging rope snapped, and I was about to fall to the cliff bottom. 
I clung tightly to the rock. Just then, a second thunderbolt struck. As I searched for a way to survive, I saw her, that strange woman, swept up by the thunderbolt, stumbling into the dark, churning water. 
She was tall and slender, not petite. But curled up like that, from a distance, she looked like an abandoned baby thrown into the water. 
I don't remember if I heard her sobs, only that she bowed her head in silence for a while, then suddenly lifted her face and shouted fiercely at the dark night sky, "Master Qu Yuan! When you threw yourself into the river, having no way to serve your country, did you also utter such a cry of utter despair?" 

Only wind and rain answered her. 

She seemed deflated, slowly sinking, letting the water surface cover her. Completely cover her. 
But just when I thought she would vanish beneath the water, suddenly, wind howled all around, phantom shadows flickered, as if countless souls traversed primordial cosmos, emitting long cries. 

"Rouge cracks into cold armor light, Jade Gate snow tempers sword-brows crimson!" The wind sounded like human speech, as if urging her to rise. 
"Say not that rosy cheeks are not iron armor, when have heroines ever yielded to men?" Her voice came from underwater, as if in response. 

A lightning bolt tore the sky. In an instant, all around became bright as day, a person stood up abruptly from the water, dragging a long dragon tail, amidst the howling wind and long cries. 
I recognized her! She was that Tang princess! 

I understand! I fully understand! Those cries that summoned her from the black waters just now must belong to Wang Zhaojun venturing beyond the frontier on a snowy night, Liu Jieyou galloping a thousand miles, Princess Wencheng knocking on Yumen's snow... belong to countless ill-fated noble daughters married far to foreign lands. 

Wind howled, the heavenly gate opened wide, torrential rain poured down. Sounds swallowed by historians' ink now all became blade-songs piercing the firmament. 
Countless princesses lifted her out of the water; and she led countless princesses, striving to climb the gate to heaven. 

Carrying the earnest hopes of a multitude, she leaped, completing this transformation into a dragon. 
And as she bowed to face the thunderstorm, they transformed into the hard scales on her back. 
Or was it really her who emerged from the water, or them? 

Together, they walked upward, toward the end of the road, returning to their origin, ascending to the sky. Amidst the torrential rain, they faced the overwhelming thunder. 

They left. 
Amidst such thunder and rain, I could no longer tell what I had seen or heard. 
What I felt, was it merely sympathy, pity, or praise for the princesses? 
No, I felt the blood flowing in my veins, the power surging in my chest. I suddenly regained immense strength, gripping the protruding rocks tightly. I would climb that high cliff. I would survive. 
I would go study, I would write poetry, I would record what I saw, so that you who read this book now may see. 
I do not know when I will die, but in the end, I did not die beneath that day's broken cliff. Nor did she.

"The Nine-Bend Yellow River guards its ford, as treasures from four seas fall from the sky."
A ford commands the river's gateway, spanning east-west and north-south—the vital throat of canal transport. When the Khitans invaded Bianliang, Zhang betrayed the state and was slain by Zhu and Feng. With the River Master's domain usurped, the Dragon Hall seized power, rising to infamy. Yet the Fates abhor excess—none remain whole, none stay joyful. After Emperor Shizong's death, the Song Dynasty replaced Zhou, and the Yellow River burst its banks at Huzi. Torrential floods swallowed all... Thus did the world turn, never to return...

The Tale of the Mysterious Hunt

Once, a hunter named Zhao Qi caught a fat rabbit in the snow. Its fur gleamed, and it felt heavier than most.
Pleased with his prize, Zhao Qi skinned it and cooked it up for a few friends. Everyone praised the meat, saying its rich fat rivaled even lamb. Zhao Qi swelled with pride.
But that night, under the cold moon, strange sounds crept from the kitchen, like the cries of a newborn beast. Zhao Qi lit a lantern, only to find claw marks lay smeared in blood by the stove. The rabbit's skin, hung from the beam, seemed to rise and fall softly, as if it were still breathing.

Three days later, Zhao Qi's belly swelled with pain. No physician could cure him.
A shaman from Qinchuan heard of his plight and suggested, "A pregnant beast carries three souls. You've taken its life, now a vengeful spirit grows inside you."

With the shaman's help, Zhao Qi finally vomited a hairy mass, shaped like a newborn rabbit.
From that day on, hunters in Qinchuan followed a rule they called the Three Rules of the Hunt:
Do not kill a pregnant beast, do not hunt on moonlit nights, and do not disturb a den with cubs inside.

打造手法\n所好者道也，进乎技矣。\n产物打造过程中需要使用手法，手法具备以下规:
Crafting Techniques:
What we value is the Dao, which transcends mere skill. 
Techniques are required for crafting. Detailed rules: 
1. Each attempt has limited energy, restricting technique usage.
2. Techniques affect outcomes differently based on the item. 
3. Techniques consume energy at varying rates.
打造规则\n开物成务，冒天下之道，如斯而已者也。\n按照配方中所需的材料和条件进:
Crafting Rules:
Creating tools to serve all under heaven. This is the way. 
Follow the materials and conditions specified in the recipe to craft corresponding items. Crafting Process Rules: 
1. Requires the item's diagram and materials. Blueprints are consumed after use. 
2. Each material has variants of differing quality. Only one quality tier can be selected per material. 
3. Requires a forge bench matching the item type. Higher-tier items demand higher-tier stations.

捞月者蠢人也。\n今先生以月教吾，吾亦以月应先生。万师以为天下月分三等，蠢亦分三:
To try to scoop the moon from the water is foolishness.
Since Master used the moon to teach me, I will answer him with the moon in turn. To my mind, under Heaven there are three kinds of moon, and three kinds of foolishness to match.
The lowest kind of fool cannot stomach crookedness, knows nothing of worldly ways, and cares nothing for wealth, yet takes chivalry for his moon and a world of wrongs for his water. He throws his courage behind the cause of righting wrongs, bares his heart and guts to keep impossible promises, wears himself down from head to toe without sparing his own body, and in the end gains no more than a scrap or two of empty fame. He does not know fear. This is the first kind of foolishness.
The middle kind of fool will not follow the tide, will not drift with the muddy current, and does not know when to advance or when to retreat. He takes the common people for his moon and an age of chaos for his water. He grieves for the rise and fall of the realm, and just as deeply for the hardships of the people. Alone, he pushes against the current, like an ant trying to shake a tree, leaving behind no more than a few faint ripples. He does not know how to change. This is the second kind of foolishness.
The highest kind of fool does not spare life or death, does not chase fame, and has no use for glory or splendor. He takes history itself for his moon and the passing years for his water. He would move a thousand mountains for the sake of generations yet to come, cast aside the needs of one age to plan for a thousand years beyond it. Like monkeys clutching one another's tails, he does not even know where it all ends. In the end, all he can scoop up is the moon's reflection in the water, flowers in a mirror, nothing that can truly be held. He does not know profit. This is the top of foolishness.
How many clever people there are in this world. Heaven and earth have no heart, and the people have no certain fate. To pray for peace for ten thousand generations is like trying to scoop the moon from the water. No wise man would do such a thing. Only fools would.
Alas. I had thought that to possess even one of these three kinds of foolishness was rare, and to possess all three rarer still. Who would have guessed that all here are such fools?
What good fortune indeed.

To the Sect Master,

By the time you find this place, I will likely already rest among the mountain stones. Please do not grieve.

To take the mountain stones into my reckoning, to borrow the winds of Heaven and Earth, and to stake my life on it... I go gladly.
To struggle for life in a hopeless place with this frail body, and though it cost me my heart's blood... I have no regret.
To enter a game that spans the ages, to cast my lot with Heaven and Earth, and though I serve only as a stepping stone... I have no regret.

Only one sorrow remains: that I shall not play one more game with you.

揉着隐隐作痛的额角，望着院里挤作一团的山民——不过七八个人，却嚷出了百来人的喧哗:
Rubbing his throbbing temples, Zhen Gui surveyed the villagers crowding his yard. There were barely eight of them, yet they kicked up a racket fit for a hundred, chirping and squawking like a flock of startled sparrows.

"Lord Zhen, you gotta give us justice! My husband's third-uncle-in-law's second-cousin-twice-removed... well, that man went and stewed my best laying hen! Said he'd pay me back with a wooden eagle, but I haven't seen a splinter of it!" 
They were treating him like some legendary magistrate, coming to him to settle their petty squabbles.

"Lord Zhen, you said you were done with this old plank, right? The wind is howling right through my shack, and I desperately need a patch..." 
Wonderful. This one was just here to scavenge.

"Lord Zhen, that medicine you helped me get last time didn't work so well. Look, my leg is still limping!" 
Great. This one was at the wrong door entirely.

The villagers' complaints and pleas poured out in a chaotic, endless stream. Zhen Gui's fingers tapped an idle rhythm on the peeling wooden table. He grunted the occasional hum to keep them going, but his gaze had long since slipped out the window, glued to the setting sun.

Three, two, one. Zhen Gui counted the heartbeats in his head. 
Who would have thought his life would tumble into this godforsaken wilderness? His old passion had cooled to ash, leaving him with nothing but the strange talent of counting sunsets down to the second. Surely, that counted as a blessing in disguise.

The moment the sun dipped behind the mountain, Zhen Gui sprang to his feet. "Sun's down! I'm officially off the clock. Go on home, folks! Hey, you! Leave that plank alone! Can't you see the characters for 'Bureau of Relief' carved right there?"
"Bureau of Beef? Now that's a fine name! Lad, go tell your mother to stop messing with that ox. We'll just come here to borrow our beef from now on!" The villagers mumbled, wandering off with satisfied grins.

Bureau of Beef? What absolute nonsense. It was the Bureau of Relief, a place meant to solve the troubles that ordinary people could not. Zhen Gui climbed up a ladder, preparing to nail the wooden sign he had just snatched back from the villager.

If he had known he would end up rotting in this mountain crevice, why did his younger self ever work so hard? It was a mistake. A huge mistake. 

All that talk about how the Special Office of Hidden Mountain needed a seasoned veteran to hold the fort. They told him that although Zhen Gui lacked mechanical ingenuity, his keen eye for detail and relentless pursuit of the truth were exactly what these wilds required. And where were the cases? Just endless trivial chores and zero resources. No manpower, no funding. He even had to carve the signboard himself.
And the people here... they simply lacked any sense of reason.

No matter how many times he corrected them, they still called him "Lord" as if he were truly some high dignitary. In reality, he was just a middle-aged head constable who had dug too deep into a major case, made enemies everywhere, and was forced to change his name and flee just to keep his head attached to his neck.

What a cruel irony. He had spent his entire life seeking justice for others, yet his own grievances had to remain buried forever in his heart. Enough of that. Had a certain someone not recommended him to Hidden Mountain, his head would be hanging from a city gate by now. 

As his mind wandered, a stray splinter from the rough wood jabbed sharply into his index finger. A faint, throbbing ache followed.
I'm done with it! No more meddling! I won't lift a finger for anything ever again! Not the big cases, and certainly not the small ones!

Zhen Gui hammered the board home with a spiteful thud. From this day forth, he swore to be like those slippery, corrupt officials who never let a conscience trouble them. If the sky falls, let the tall men catch it. Let the petty trifles slide. As for the rest of the mess, if you stall long enough, it will simply rot away on its own. 
Smart! That was the way. Half a lifetime of exhaustion was more than enough. Tomorrow, he would sleep until the sun burned his backside!

...

Night fell, bringing a chill mountain breeze. With the lamp lit, Zhen Gui held up his hand, grimacing as he tried to pry out the offending splinter. Suddenly, a faint rustle stirred outside the window.
He knew someone was out there. He always knew. Hmph. Ever since he had crawled into this forgotten corner, he had not enjoyed a single night of peace. There were no grand cases here, only endless family drama. God knows whose ancient history he would have to endure until midnight this time.

He swung the door open, only to find a few children nudging and shoving one another, creeping forward with timid steps.

"L-Lord Zhen... my dad asked me to bring you this... medicine oil. He saw you rubbing your forehead this afternoon, and said this works great for headaches..." The boy at the front spoke in a voice smaller than a mosquito's.

A night breeze drifted past, carrying the raw, herbal scent of the oil into the quiet mountain darkness.
Zhen Gui froze. He reached out and accepted the crude earthenware bottle, then turned back inside to fetch his oil lamp for the children.

Standing at the threshold, he watched that tiny speck of light sway and bob until the vast night finally swallowed it whole. Right then, a few birds called out nearby.

Zhen Gui looked up. Beneath the crumbling edge of the eaves, a new nest had appeared. It was small, yet firmly nestled against the wooden beam.
Strange. He could have sworn the hot blood in his chest had long since turned to ash... 
Yet at this very moment, why did that old, familiar warmth come flooding back?

Fine. Perhaps he could tolerate this Bureau of Relief for a few more days. Just a few.

Mention Big Zhao anywhere in Kaifeng, and you'll hear nothing but praise. 

Though he wasn't often seen, those who did run into him were almost always in luck. Doesn't matter if you're close or just an acquaintance—if you've run into trouble and mention it to him, he'll go out of his way to pull strings and find someone who can help. Ask him how he pulled it off, and he just gives you a quiet smile. Eventually, the neighbors started spinning their own tales. Wild guesses about who he really was, where he came from, what kind of hidden background he might have. 

And yet, every time they saw him again, that plain, honest face always made them doubt their own imaginations. Could someone like him really be some high-born noble?

Whether or not to implement the Tang Coin Confiscation Policy weighed heavily on Zhao Kuangyin's mind.

The circulation of Tang coins in Song territory was no secret, a strategic move by Jiangnan to maintain influence. But confiscating them was no simple task: Tang coins had become a backbone of Song currency. Banning them overnight would amount to stripping wealth from the people, sure to ignite resentment. In peacetime, replacing them with Song copper coins might soften the blow, but with internal rebellions in Jinghu demanding immediate military response and war funds still lacking, how could the court afford to reimburse citizens?
Ultimately, Zhao Kuangyin concluded that long-term pain was preferable to prolonged crisis. Confiscating Tang coins without reimbursement would secure quick victories in Jinghu, followed by campaigns to conquer Jiangnan and Shu. Only after unification could wealth be restored to the people, a harsh but necessary strategy.
Yet no one dared voice this plan aloud, for harming public trust risked undermining the dynasty's foundation.

—Except Zhao Guangyi. As their eyes met, Zhao Kuangyin was transported back to a dawn years prior, when his young brother had earnestly repeated the creed he held dear:
"Great benevolence requires sacrificing small virtues. To hold power is to bear its responsibilities."

救不了己的人，救不了旁人。朱鱼倒是觉得，这话得反过来：救不了旁人的人，才救不了己:
One who cannot save themselves cannot save others. Zhu Yu had always thought it should be the other way around. Those who cannot save others are the ones who truly cannot save themselves. Kaifeng's Zheng Manor was no longer a house of prestige, though still whispered about for its charity. They said the young heir often gave dry rations to passing beggars to fill their stomachs. Zhu Yu herself had once received a bundle of bread from his hand.

Before she left Silver Needle, her master often said kindness is the rarest virtue in a world torn by chaos. Back then, Zhu Yu hadn't fully understood. Only after her long journey to Kaifeng, after witnessing all she had witnessed, did she truly grasp it. Kindness was rare not because people were born wicked, but because, in troubled times, kindness struggled hardest to survive. Some kindnesses were slaughtered by violence. Far more perished under the weight of human hearts turning cruel. Sometimes, Zhu Yu could no longer tell. Was it the cruelty of the world that destroyed the goodness in people? Or the cruelty of people that destroyed the goodness of the world?

That child had survived the blades. But whether he could survive the malice in men's hearts, Zhu Yu did not know. The fire raged on, devouring the Zheng Family's century of splendor, along with countless restless souls. Amid the sea of flames, a thin figure knelt alone, his frail spine stubbornly straight. His gaze flickered in the leaping firelight, wavering, then slowly sank into shadow, like an Asura who finally made up a terrible resolve. Would this child survive the evil of the human heart? 

"Waaah—"

Before Zhu Yu could ponder further, a newborn's cry pierced the ruins. Dawn had broken. The long-lost sunlight lit up a hidden bundle, a tiny swaddled baby and a rattling toy. It lit the bloodstains on Zhu Yu's sword. It lit the darkness clouding the child's eyes. Wiping the blood from her face, Zhu Yu sheathed her sword and reached out her hand.

"Zhu Yu of Qingxi."

"Zheng E... of Xingyang."

When Squarewall Hold was built is unknown, but its disappearance is deeply etched in the hearts of every Western Regions inhabitant. 
As a key military stronghold near Jade Gate Pass, it was the first place seized by the Bodchen after the great sandstorm. As if marking the start of everything, from the day it was occupied, the entire Western Regions gradually eroded under sandstorms. People tried countless times to retake Squarewall Hold but all failed, until the bloody battle occurred.

旄、节、旌、旗为中国古代礼仪制度中的重要仪仗标识。\n节为君主行使特殊使命的凭信:
In ancient China, mao (banner tassels), jie (tally tokens), jing (ceremonial flags), and qi (flags) held great significance within the rituals of state. 
The jie was a royal token of authority, while the mao was a yak-tail-adorned pole; together as maojie, they symbolized military command. The jing were flags, and the qi were silk flags marking rank and directing armies. 
Over time, their distinctions blurred, and all were collectively called maojie, representing power, military command, and status.

Few people knew that what she feared most was the cold.
Perhaps she had known too much warmth in this life. Those who waited for her were always willing to leave a lantern burning; no matter how heavy the night dew grew, she never felt the chill.
...Until this place was reduced to ruins, and she failed too many of those who had waited.
No matter how cold it became, she had to travel alone through the bone-chilling flow of time.
She had to return to the past, to every day she had missed.

Oh, world, why can we not return to the very beginning?

To make all of it stop, she never allowed herself to stop.
Now, it is all over.
She met the one who had come from the present.
The array she sought to protect was finally safe and sound.
She no longer needed to walk forward, nor did she need to walk back.
